about: The follow-up register: every task a round finds and does not do. Rules and CLI: agentic_core/plan_followups.py, scripts/followups.py. Slots: a delivery-plan item (P2.6) or OWNER (waits on an Owner decision; never scheduled into a round). NEXT was retired in W469: a row rides an open plan item, chosen by 'routes' (first matching route in order wins: a file prefix ending '/' or an exact file, or whole lowercase words of the title) when added with --slot auto. 'done P1.13 --by W470' marks an item done and moves its riders along the routes. PLAN NOW (the generated block in the prompt and living plan §6.4) says what is next. Enforced by test_w462_followup_register_is_scheduled_and_in_lockstep and test_w469_the_plan_carries_every_followup_and_keeps_itself_current.

items.title: Transformation stage verification honest — not-assessable stages, twin persistence, validated only on an allowed gate
items.why: stages 5/6 were constant True, a halted or partial gate still validated, and a validated run moves the Owner's living-plan objectives

items.title: A blocked transfer can re-approve an approval an EARLIER action already spent
items.why: _materiality_gate returns None both below the threshold (nothing consumed) and after consuming an approval, and the blocked-transfer paths call _restore_consumed_approval unconditionally, which re-approves the latest implemented record with the matching title — so a blocked non-material transfer can hand the next material transfer a spent approval
items.source: W462 register review (read, not yet reproduced)

items.title: test_fabric_organism_systems_run_real is order-dependent
items.why: it fails when run alone (also at 1bde2eb0) and passes inside the full suite — it leans on state an earlier test leaves behind, so a green suite says nothing about it

items.title: The compliance mandates docs claim ENFORCED on a file W460 deleted
items.why: docs/compliance/MANDATES.md and MANDATES_FINAL.md list 'GaaS-Validated Mutations — ENFORCED' in packages/shared/gaas.ts, which never validated anything and no longer exists; the other ENFORCED rows need the same reading
items.source: W460 refutation (ruled out of that round's scope)

items.title: The /api/v1/swarm router carries no auth dependency
items.why: agentic_core/api/swarm.py has zero Depends — the org cascade (POST /cascade), CEO delegation (POST /delegate), proposed-catalogue curation and the run histories are callable by anyone when AUTH_ENABLED is on; P2.6 names 'swarm' among its routers, this row pins the routes

items.title: The org cascade's governance verdict gates a constant string, not the delivery
items.why: swarm.py's _attest returns a fixed attestation sentence, so 'gov: allowed' can never reflect the delivered content; W460 relabelled the chip 'intent only' — the real fix is gating the delivery itself

items.title: One violation trips the shared circuit breaker, and anyone can reset it
items.why: record_event trips on a single is_violation (no threshold), halting every later action on the node; POST /api/v1/gaas/breaker/reset has no user dependency

items.title: swarm_cascades.json writers are not under store_lock
items.why: define, update and delete load-modify-save the store with no lock — a threaded probe during the P1.12 audit lost 38 of 40 concurrent writes

items.title: The swarm HTTP contract drops per-stage model; runs have no run_id or UEG record
items.why: SwarmStageSpec carries role and instruction only, so a stage's model choice is silently discarded; run_swarm records the outcome under stage 1's served_by alone and writes no run id or ledger entry

items.title: Saved cascades cannot be deleted from the designer page
items.why: DELETE /api/v1/resources/swarm/{sid} exists but the /native-ai designer offers no way to call it

items.title: Command Center still carries hard-coded status text
items.why: 'in WORK mode for 4 hours', '3D Holographic Engine — Loading...' and 'Real-time stream initializing via libp2p...' are literals nothing measures (not compliance claims, so outside P1.12); no plan item covers packages/ui literals (P2.4's scatter is unreached backend operations)

items.title: A Board ratification queue for changes that need ratification
items.why: W459 deleted requires_ratification rather than give it a consumer; whether the Board ratifies HIGH/CRITICAL changes is a product decision

items.title: Should Change Control decisions write to the UEG?
items.why: adding a UEG write to the CCA changes what the constitutional ledger holds; the Sanctum copy stopped claiming one in W459

items.title: Change Control tier map — code_change and economy_material fall to MEDIUM by default
items.why: _TIER_MAP has no entry for them, so their risk tier is an accident of the default rather than a decision

items.title: Concurrent settles of one service contract can pay twice
items.why: settle_contract loads vsb_contracts.json, checks status delivered, awaits inter_vsb_transfer with a fresh transfer_id, then saves — no store_lock and no claim on the contract, so two concurrent settles both pass the status check and both debit the client (accept and deliver share the unlocked load-await-save shape)

items.title: Owner-payment accrue and payout write their store without store_lock
items.why: accrue (heartbeat cycles) and payout (API) load-modify-save the shared owner-payments store with no lock — the shared-store concurrency class fixed for the ledger and fund stores in W442/W444; a payout can overdraw or an accrual be lost

items.title: A marketplace purchase can charge the buyer without recording the sale
items.why: consume_tokens runs before the listing save and the receipt write; if either raises there is no refund, so the buyer is charged for a sale nothing records (consume-without-compensation)

items.title: The optimizer's resource fabric releases resources a pool never consumed
items.why: assemble_pool records the full requirements even when it could not decrement capacity, and disassemble_pool gives all of them back (gpu available 1064 of 64 at unit level); the optimizer engine assembles and releases per call
items.source: W463 class sweep (reproduced at unit level)

items.title: The evolution apply's claim release is a status-only compare-and-set
items.why: apply_approved_evolution's _release flips implemented back to approved whenever the status is implemented, without proving the implemented state is this caller's own claim (no claim nonce) — the shape W463 removed from the economy restore; not reachable today

items.title: genome_engine.py is unimported and its rollback restores by position
items.why: GenomeMutationWorkflow.rollback pops the LAST checkpoint instead of the proposal's, does not persist, and references an undefined GENOME_FILE; nothing imports the module, but layer_registry names the l1_identity directory by path — archive only after the Owner's WIRED-map check

items.title: store_lock ignores its timeout when a stale lockfile cannot be removed
items.why: In the stale branch (lockfile older than stale_after) store_lock tries to unlink it and `continue`s whether or not the unlink worked, skipping both the deadline check and the sleep; when the unlink keeps failing, a waiter loops without sleeping until the file goes away, so the documented bounded timeout does not apply. W463 adds callers on the transfer path (debit_posted no longer locks, but record_transfer and the gate lock do). Fix: continue only when the unlink succeeded; otherwise fall through to the deadline check. Guard: a lockfile aged past stale_after that cannot be unlinked times out within timeout.

items.title: A heartbeat cycle posts before it consumes its events, so a failed consume distributes them twice
items.why: operate_vsb runs governed_cycle_sync (run_cycle writes the ledger) and only then consume_events. If consume_events raises (its store_lock timed out while another writer held revenue_events.json.lock for over 10s, or the write kept failing), operate_vsb returns an error with the cycle already posted and the events still pending; the next beat posts the same events again (reproduced by the W463 refuter with a real held lockfile: one 1000-WST event posted twice). A material cycle's approval stays spent and the next beat files a hold for revenue already distributed. Pre-existing ordering (W313); W463 only changed which ids are consumed. Fix: consume inside governed_cycle_sync after every gate passes and before run_cycle, size the cycle from what was consumed, un-consume those exact ids if run_cycle raises.

items.title: A transfer whose receiver queue write fails twice is left debited with nothing to repair it
items.why: record_transfer debits the sender and queues the receiver in two steps. If the queue write fails on the first attempt and again on the endpoint's single idempotent replay (e.g. the pending-transfers lock held for over 20s), POST /economy/transfer returns 500 with no transfer_id: the sender stays debited, the receiver is never credited, nothing anywhere replays that transfer_id, and a client retry mints a new id and pays again (a material one files a fresh hold). A process that dies between the two steps strands the debit the same way. For a non-material transfer no economy UEG event records it. Pre-existing (the same at c519c497); W463 keeps the approval spent and no longer tells the Owner to re-approve. Fix: reconcile stranded legs (sender postings naming a transfer_id with no pending-store entry are replayed through record_transfer, which is idempotent) on the heartbeat or next access; answer the endpoint with the transfer_id and a debited-receiver-pending status instead of a bare 500; log the non-material case.

items.title: A rejected contract settlement tells the client to retry after a hold that does not exist
items.why: When settle_contract's transfer comes back rejected_by_change_control, it still returns 'settlement HELD by governance — retry after the hold clears', stores settlement.held=True, and ServiceContracts.tsx shows that note and a 'settlement held' badge. No hold exists — the rejection answers exactly that action — and the price and receiver are fixed, so every retry is refused again while that rejection is the newest decided record for the pair. The page also ignores the new rejected_by field. Pre-existing (found by the W463 sixth refutation). Fix: branch on governance.status == 'rejected_by_change_control', say what rejected it (the same wording map as VSBEconomy/TransferPanel) and that retrying the same price is refused; render that on ServiceContracts.tsx.

items.title: test_v191_evolution_approvals_route_through_change_control is order-dependent
items.why: it passes alone and in the full suite order but fails after the organism-status tests (the same -k selection fails at b97e38e7): its LOW proposal is only auto-approved when composite health is at least 0.6, and an earlier test leaves the organism less healthy, so the approval stays under_change_control and the re-approve answer is 'Already with the Change Control Agency.' — the same class as FU-003
items.source: W464 (found in passing, reproduced at HEAD)

items.title: config/paths.py resolves BASE_DIR one level above the repository
items.why: BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent is the repo's parent (C:/Users/rehan), so without WORKSTATION_DATA_DIR the live MEMORY_FILE, INTERACTIONS_DB, L7 registry, meeting log and chroma store live in <repo-parent>/data and ensure_dirs() creates logs/genome/models directories there at import (ai/memory.py, ai/logger.py, v138 ceo, synthesis, ingestion, qep_flagship import it). Fixing the path relocates the live AI memory store: migrate it deliberately (copy, verify, switch), never move it silently

items.title: MANDATES.md certifies a 1127-article genome that does not exist
items.why: docs/compliance/MANDATES.md and MANDATES_FINAL.md mark '1127-Article Genome' VERIFIED, 'seeded in genome/constitution.work and Merkle-DAG'; no such file exists and the genome engine's seed holds 3 articles — a false VERIFIED claim beside FU-004's false ENFORCED rows

items.title: genome_engine's self-healing cycle would ratify a fixed template, and its validator reads a CWD-relative file at import
items.why: GenomeMutationWorkflow.run_self_healing_cycle applies ConstitutionalAI.generate_amendment's fixed template with authorized=True (unreachable today only because the validator's PQC rule refuses its context), and validator.py builds validator_l1 at import from the CWD-relative genome/constitution.work, which the engine no longer writes; both stay unwired (the Owner kept the module unwired, W464)

items.title: Board ratification is apex-only, and the Board's other routes trust a client-supplied owner
items.why: GET/POST /api/v1/board/ratifications cover every change (admin under auth; on_owner_direction in both modes) — a VSB-scoped change is not routed to that VSB's own board or tenant owner; board.py's chief/instruct and directive still take 'owner' from the request body and carry no auth dependency (the P2.6 perimeter)

items.title: In single-user mode a HIGH override needs no acknowledgement, so it skips Board ratification
items.why: with auth off any client's override_decision is recorded as admin_override (the Owner's explicit decision) and a HIGH change approved that way is not queued for ratification; CRITICAL requires admin_decision_for_critical, HIGH requires nothing

items.title: A decision whose ledger write failed leaves no mark on the record, and nothing reconciles it
items.why: Change Control writes a decision's UEG node after the record lands (W464, FU-013); a failed write or a process that dies in between leaves the decision without a node, reported only in that response (ueg_logged false) and the server log — the record carries nothing a later reconciliation could find, so the gap is invisible after the response

items.title: The audit views read an Owner's rejection as a fault
items.why: classify_event flags cca.change_rejected and board.change_ratification_refused (a refusal); the Governance Hub shows them red FLAGGED and counts them with failures without rendering flag.why, and ConstitutionalUI's UEG tab ignores flag entirely (tone keyed to two event types)

items.title: A review of a change record missing rationale, affected_systems or rollback_plan answers 500
items.why: review_change builds its prompt with c['rationale'], c['affected_systems'] and c['rollback_plan'] — a record written without them (hand-written or by an older writer) raises KeyError after _start has already moved it to under_review

items.title: A service contract can be offered to an entity that is not living, and nothing declines or cancels one
items.why: offer_contract never checks that the client and provider are registered living entities: the W465 probe offered a contract to a provider id that exists nowhere, accepted it, and delivered it (a whole provider-scoped org cascade ran — 15-25 minutes on a local model) before settle refused the transfer with 404. There is no decline for the provider or cancel for the client, so such a contract sits 'delivered' forever. Fix: validate both parties at offer (and again at accept), add decline/cancel with their own UEG events, and let the page offer them.

items.title: A settlement's materiality approval is bound to the client-provider pair, not to the contract
items.why: A contract settlement goes through the transfer gate, which binds an approval to the sender, the counterparty and an amount ceiling (W463). Two material contracts between the same client and provider therefore share one hold identity: the Owner's approval of contract A's settlement releases contract B's settlement of an equal or smaller price if B settles first, and A is then asked again. Virtual WST. Fix: carry the contract id into the gate's action identity (source 'contract:<id>') so a hold, an approval and a rejection name exactly one contract.

items.title: A failed owner accrual is reported but never re-applied, so the Owner's balance stays short
items.why: Since W465 a cycle whose owner accrual fails says so (owner_accrual.accrued false, economy.owner_accrual_failed on the UEG, an error log) — but nothing re-applies the missing credit: the ledger shows the owner stage distributed while owner payments never received it. Fix: record the failed accrual durably (the UEG event carries vsb, amount and cycle), and reconcile on the next successful accrual or heartbeat — re-apply each unreconciled failure once, idempotent on its cycle id.

items.title: A second delivery of the same contract runs a whole cascade before it is refused
items.why: deliver_contract binds its result with a compare-and-set only after the cascade returns (W465), so a second Deliver while the first runs starts a second provider-scoped org cascade (15-25 minutes on a local model) whose work is then discarded with 409 'another delivery bound first'. Fix: claim the delivery before the cascade (as settle claims), release it if the cascade raises.

items.title: A pending-transfers record with the wrong inner types debits the sender, then fails with a 500
items.why: W465 refuses a pending store that is unreadable or not an object before any debit, but a record inside it with the wrong types (a number for the record, pending_wst 'x', transfers 'abc' or [1]) passes that check; the debit posts and record_transfer then raises AttributeError/TypeError after it (the same before W465). The approval stays spent correctly and a settle's retry completes it, but a plain transfer answers 500 with a stranded debit. Fix: validate each record's shape in _read_pending (refuse with PendingStoreUnavailable) so the refusal comes before the debit.

items.title: A settle that raises leaves the previous attempt's unpaid outcome on the contract
items.why: settle_contract records an outcome only when the transfer answers; any exception exit (a crash after the debit, a 503 from the ledger or the pending store) releases the claim and leaves the settlement field of an EARLIER attempt, so the page can still show 'held for the Owner' after the Owner approved and the latest attempt failed for another reason. Nothing is paid twice and settling again completes it. Fix: on an exception exit, record outcome 'unknown' with the error (inside the release mutation), and let the page say settle again.

items.title: A cycle swallows a failed venture-returns intake silently, and the Board page cites a server log it may not have
items.why: W465 made a failed inter-VSB receipts intake visible (inter_vsb_receipts_error, a warning log) and made the gate measure only receipts the intake can take; consume_pending_returns in the same cycle still swallows every error as 0 recycled with no report or log, and its peek may read differently. Separately BoardOfDirectors.tsx tells the Owner to 'see the server log' when a ratification's ledger entry did not land — check that the server logs that case (the W465 owner-accrual alert did not until the third refutation).

items.title: A VSB ledger that cannot be read is replaced by empty books on the next posting
items.why: VirtualLedger's writers load tolerantly (ledger.py:59-81): a ledger with a BOM, or one that does not parse, reads as empty books, and the next posting writes them back — every posting and balance gone, including the transfer_out debits that settle retries and transfer replays read as evidence (reproduced: 2 postings became 1, reserve 495 became 1). The same class W465 closed for the pending-transfers, contract and owner-payments stores. Fix: a strict read for every writer (refuse, never overwrite) with the route answering 503.

items.title: The constitutional ledger's chain is replaced when its file cannot be read
items.why: UEGLogger._read is tolerant (ueg.py:136-141): one log call on a chain file with a BOM or a parse failure replaced 5 nodes with 1 (reproduced) — the append-only, hash-chained audit trail every governance claim cites is silently restarted. Fix: a strict read in the writer that refuses (and reports the refusal to the caller, whose ueg_logged then reads false) rather than starting a new chain over the old one.

items.title: The revenue-events store is wiped when unreadable, and its cap drops events still pending
items.why: revenue.py:34-35 reads tolerantly, so one record_event on a store with a BOM kept 1 event of 2000 (reproduced); and rows[-2000:] (revenue.py:52/104/133) drops the oldest events whether consumed or not — a held VSB's pending 5000-WST event vanished after one new event elsewhere (reproduced). Fix with FU-022: strict reads for writers, and a cap that drops only consumed events.

items.title: A cycle that raises at its first ledger write has already drained receipts and returns, which reach no ledger
items.why: run_cycle drains venture returns and inter-VSB receipts (metabolism.py:116-136) before its first ledger write (:148); if that write raises, the drained amounts are gone from their queues and posted nowhere (reproduced: a 300-WST receipt vanished). Fix with FU-022: record what was drained and give it back when nothing was written.

items.title: The heartbeat drops a failed entity visit silently, and revenue.consume_pending is ungated dead code
items.why: heartbeat.py:239-243 discards operate_vsb's error result, so a failed or partly posted non-material cycle leaves no trace anywhere (reproduced); and revenue.consume_pending (revenue.py:108-134) has no callers yet would consume every pending event without any gate if one were added. Fix: log the failed visit (UEG + log) and delete the dead function.

items.title: A receiver id containing ' — ' would make a transfer's replay debit again
items.why: W465 anchored _memo_names on the system memo head, split at the first ' — ' (transfers.py _memo_names), so a posting to a receiver whose id contains ' — ' is not recognised as its own debit and a replay of that id debits again. Generated ids are vsb-<hex>; whether any path registers a caller-chosen id (vsb.py:1431 takes entity.get('vsb_id')) is unverified. Fix: FU-023's structured marker on the posting (the id stored as data, not parsed from text), or refuse such ids at registration.
items.source: W466 pre-audit (by reading) — a W465 regression

items.title: A transfer stranded before W466 can only be found by hand
items.why: W466 completes a stranded transfer (the sender debited, the receiver never credited) only when its debit carries the receiver-leg marker written since W466: a debit made earlier cannot prove whether its receiver was credited once its id left the receiver's 50-row display window (and before W465 no durable credited-id list existed), so completing it could credit the receiver twice. POST /transfers/{id}/complete refuses such a debit (409) and the pass never lists it. Fix, if any exist: a one-off Owner-reviewed audit listing unmarked transfer_out debits with no credited-id and no display-window entry, completed individually on the Owner's decision.
items.source: W466 pre-audit (reproduced: replaying an old id re-credited it)

items.title: A heartbeat cycle whose process stopped mid-cycle leaves the Owner's approval spent and asks again
items.why: W467 consumes a cycle's recognised events before it runs; if the process is killed between that consume and the cycle's first ledger write, the stranded-consume pass (every fifth beat with autonomous economy on) gives the events back after 15 minutes, but a material cycle's approval stays implemented without a released_action_ran marker (it reads as still in flight — the restrictive side), so the next beat files a fresh CRITICAL hold for the same events and the Owner decides twice. The economy.cycle_intake_consumed record names the approval's cca_id and consume_id. Fix: when the pass gives back a token's events, restore that approval if its trail has no released_action_ran for that consume_id (the W463 give-back rules).
items.source: W467 first refutation (reproduced by killing a process)

items.title: An unreadable compliance-history file lifts every FAIL hold
items.why: living_vsbs._latest_screen and list_living read vsb_compliance_history.json with load_json_tolerant: a file with a BOM (or one that does not parse) reads as {}, so operate_vsb sees no FAIL screen and runs distribution cycles for entities whose latest screen FAILED, and the roster shows them never screened. Since W468 a visit that raises also drops a compliance_fail_hold (reaching the cycle is taken as proof the screen is not FAIL), which is only true while the history reads. Fix: a strict read; an unreadable history holds every entity whose screen cannot be known.

items.title: The living-VSB roster is replaced when its file cannot be read
items.why: living_vsbs._load returns {} for any read failure, and register() then writes back a roster holding only the new entity (a BOM roster kept 1 of 3 entries), so the heartbeat stops tending every other entity. Also operate_one's sort calls int() on every entry's operating_cycles, so one corrupt entry stops the rotation for all. Fix: a strict read for every writer (register, deregister, _update_entry); refuse, never overwrite; skip a malformed entry with a record.

items.title: The Owner's waterfall overrides are replaced when their file cannot be read
items.why: metabolism._load_waterfall_overrides answers {} on any failure and POST /economy/waterfall saves without a lock or an atomic write: one save on an unreadable store kept only the new override, and a cycle on an unreadable store silently uses the template (waterfall_source entity_template). Fix: strict, locked, atomic; a cycle says when the override store could not be read.

items.title: The venture portfolio is replaced when its file cannot be read
items.why: ventures._load_portfolio is tolerant: record_positions on an unreadable portfolio kept only the new position, losing holdings and pending returns. Fix: a strict read for every writer.

items.title: More stores are read tolerantly and then written back
items.why: Same class as FU-041, found by reading: agent_hub post_message/register_agent/update_handoff_status, integration_surface.spawn_twin, resource_fabric.run_composition, swarm curate and cascade, heartbeat.screen_living_vsb, and config.mutate_json (no callers). Each answers empty on a failed read and saves over the store. Fix: one strict-read helper for writers, applied store by store.

items.title: A failed UEG write inside the constitutional interceptor turns a decided action into an exception
items.why: uci_v16_omega.intercept writes to the UEG unprotected (policy halt, execution failure, checkpoint): when that write raises (an unreadable chain, a store lock timeout) intercept raises, so board chief_instruct re-runs its action, governed_cycle reports ungated_bypass_logged although the gate allowed it, a transfer that posted answers 500 and genesis journeys 500. It also records any action exception as a circuit-breaker failure, and when its execution_failure log raises, that error replaces the action's own (a /cycle LedgerUnavailable then answers 500). Fix: the interceptor wraps its own UEG writes (ueg_logged on the result; blocked stays blocked; the original exception is re-raised). Pairs with FU-042.

items.title: The default UEG path is relative to the working directory
items.why: ueg.py resolves its default chain path relative to CWD, so a backend started from another directory starts a separate chain (found by reading). Fix: resolve through config.data_path.

items.title: An unreadable VSB ledger has no repair path
items.why: W468 refuses an unreadable ledger for good (every cycle, close and transfer answers 503) and the pages say to try again once it can be read, but nothing in the product can make it readable: a stray BOM, a truncation or a pre-W442 NaN posting needs a hand edit. Fix: an admin repair (copy to quarantine, a lossless re-read or the valid prefix, UEG-logged with what was lost), like FU-042's chain recovery.

items.title: A transfer refused on a retry says nothing was debited although an earlier attempt may have
items.why: _transfer_core answers any SenderLedgerUnavailable with X-Transfer-Debited: false and 'Nothing was debited' (true of this request only): a settlement retried under its persisted transfer id, whose first attempt debited, is told nothing was debited once the ledger becomes unreadable. And a gated action that raised is retried outside the gate (W463 design), so a refusal inside the action runs again ungated. Fix: say 'this attempt debited nothing; an earlier attempt under this id may have' and keep the retry inside the gate's decision.

items.title: A cycle whose ledger write times out answers a bare 500
items.why: /cycle maps only LedgerUnavailable (503) and LedgerWriteRefused (409): a store_lock TimeoutError or a PermissionError from atomic_write_json during a cycle's writes still escapes as a 500 with no statement of what was written; the async governed_cycle writes no economy.cycle_raised record when its cycle raises (the heartbeat path does); and the strict read's retry sleeps block the event loop in async routes. Fix: map them with the ledger_written wording, and move the retries off the loop.

items.title: The economy pages keep earlier figures beside a new refusal
items.why: VSBEconomy.runCycle and VSBCockpit leave the previous cycle's report and balances on screen under a refused or partly written cycle; the cockpit shows nothing for a 200 hold (cycle null), its other actions (growth, chief, transformation, deliverables, ship state) are not tied to the selected entity, avatars/api.py reads the raw roster hold (stale after a repair, and blind to decision_hold and last_error), and doClosePeriod parses a non-JSON error body as JSON. Fix: clear or label the stale figures, render the hold, and guard every entity-scoped load as W468 guarded the ledger.

items.title: A development spend posts as a distribution and two spends can overdraw the fund
items.why: spend_self_investment checks the balance on the construction snapshot and records under the lock without re-checking, so two concurrent spends each draw the whole balance (self_investment goes negative); and record('self_investment', kind='debit') posts Dr distribution_self_investment / Cr cash, the same as a distribution, so a spend increases the distribution expense; a spend that fails for any other reason (a busy ledger lock) is recorded nowhere. Fix: check inside the lock and post a development-spend account.

items.title: Books near the float limit: a period close saves and then answers 500
items.why: With balances near 1.7e308 WST (only a crafted or imported ledger reaches this; cycle inputs are bounded at 1e15 since W468), close_period's statement sums overflow to inf: the close marker is saved with an Infinity net profit and the route answers a bare 500 (JSON cannot carry inf). The ledger's save check covers balances and posting amounts, not the close marker's figures. Fix: compute the statements before saving and refuse (LedgerWriteRefused, 409) when any figure is not finite.

items.title: A revenue event can record a non-finite amount
items.why: revenue.record_event does not check that amount_wst is finite, so a NaN or inf event would be written to a store its own strict reader then refuses, or distributed into a ledger the ledger then refuses to save. Fix: refuse non-finite amounts at record_event.

items.title: Visit outcomes are reported inconsistently across heartbeat, genesis and pages
items.why: heartbeat counts a held or refused visit (ledger_unavailable, compliance or governance hold) as an operate_vsb action and sets last_vsb_operated; genesis's streaming establish says 'cycle ran' for an operate_vsb result that has only an error, and a result {error, cycle_ran True} (a cycle that posted and whose roster bookkeeping raised) is counted as not operated; list_living shows statuses that are not holds (intake_unavailable, intake_consumed_elsewhere) as 'held by governance'; a gate-error hold (no Change Control record) is kept on a raise as if it were a decision; the compliance branch's roster write sits outside the try (a raise there leaves last_operated unchanged); and two visits of one entity at once can clobber each other's row. Fix: report held, refused, raised and ran as four outcomes everywhere. Related to FU-045.

items.title: The roster's ledger-hold text reads every held entity's whole ledger on each call
items.why: list_living describes a ledger_unavailable hold from a live strict read of that entity's ledger; the heartbeat and pages call it often, and with large ledgers this is seconds per call (4 s for 60 held rows of 4 MB, measured). Negligible at today's sizes. Fix: cache by the file's size and mtime.

items.title: A ledger that keeps reserves only in the legacy balances refuses every transfer
items.why: A ledger written before W256 holds entries and balances but no accounts: validate_transfer reads reserve_fund from accounts (0.0) and refuses any transfer as insufficient funds, although the legacy view shows reserves. Fix: say the ledger predates double entry, or migrate it once.

items.title: A W463 test leaves a half-written ledger in the shared test store
items.why: test_w463 (around line 10975) writes a '{ half-written' ledger under uid 'broken' and never removes it, so every later reconcile pass in the same store counts one unreadable ledger. Fix: remove it in the test's cleanup.

items.title: close and drop rewrite a row that is already closed
items.why: followups.py close sets status done and closed_by on any row, and drop sets dropped and its note, without checking the row is open: closing FU-001 again with --by W470 silently rewrites the round that closed it, and drop turns a done row dropped. Fix: refuse unless the row is open (a reopen command if one is ever needed).

items.title: reslot --gate silently ignores --slot
items.why: reslot FU-007 --gate --slot P2.1 slots the row OWNER and drops the --slot without a word. Fix: refuse --slot with --gate, or say it was ignored.

items.title: A plain done word in a plan item's first line reads as a malformed done marker
items.why: plan_items flags malformed_done when _DONE_MENTION (a check mark, or the word done not followed by when) appears anywhere in the rest of an item's first line, so a new item whose text says, for example, 'counted as done only when verified' or 'not done by the floor' fails check as if its marker were malformed, and mark_done refuses it. Fix: look for a done marker only right after the id and the bracket, not in the prose.

items.title: Plan item texts keep hand-written rider lists that drift from the register
items.why: P2.6's text says register rows FU-005, FU-006 and FU-007 ride it; since W469 nine do. Other items name their riders by hand too. Fix: item texts point at PLAN NOW and the rendered schedule instead of listing rows, or check() compares any FU ids an item names with the rows riding it.
items.source: W469 second refutation (refuted as a W469 defect, real as drift)

items.title: Nine source-pointer product directories are still listed as products of a kind
items.why: The catalogue now marks them status source ('a pointer, nothing served yet') and no consumer builds from them, but products/ still holds nine metadata.json directories (business_incubator, cognitive_scraper, gse, molecular_sdk, nanophotonic_navigation, scraping_suite, uviap, mjm-intelligence-engine, signature-product-suite) whose only substance is a pointer at SDK source. Fix: for each, either serve it (a route and a real page) or retire the directory; the scatter item decides which, per the reach audit.

items.title: The six legacy signature-product directories still sit in products/ with self-declaring manifests
items.why: products/Care … products/Science each carry a manifest.json self-declaring PRODUCTION_READY, WCAG 2.2 AAA and nine injection formats that nothing serves; W470 lists them as legacy archives and routes nothing to them, but the directories remain where a reader takes them for products. Fix: move them to _archive/products/ (LEGACY_ARCHIVES then empties) and keep one line in the catalogue saying they were archived.

items.title: A done --hand-to merge lifts the taker's own broad matchers to the handed route's position
items.why: merge_routes (W469 refutation 2) places the merged route at the EARLIEST position of the routes merged so the handed area keeps its precedence — but the taker's original matchers move with it: done P1.13 --hand-to P1.16 put P1.16's broad prefixes (integration_tests/, docs/, …) at position 1, ahead of every specific route, so a docs+economy row would have gone to hygiene instead of P2.9. W470 re-added P1.16 last by hand and gave P1.13's area to P2.4. Fix: keep the taker's route where it was and carry only the handed matchers forward — either a second route for the same item marked handed_from, or a per-matcher position; and check() should refuse a merge that would move a route holding a directory prefix broader than the handed one ahead of any other route.
items.source: W470 (found by running done P1.13 --hand-to P1.16)

items.title: The Cockpit's plan tab has no owner-edit surface and no owner-edited marks
items.why: W471 wired the owner-edit form (POST /business-plan/set with clear) and the owner-edited marks into BusinessPlan.tsx only; VSBCockpit's plan tab shows the Chief's Opening with its provenance badge and pending list but the founder cannot set or clear a field there and set fields are not marked. Fix: mount the same edit form and marks on the Cockpit's plan tab (one component shared by both pages).

items.title: Read-only readers still use load_json_tolerant; retire the tolerant loader once every writer is strict
items.why: W472 made every WRITER read strictly (config.read_json_strict). The read-only readers that summarise or list — revenue._load (pending_summary), ueg._read (recent), agent_hub listing reads, integration_surface listings, resource_fabric composition/swarm listings, swarm proposed_catalogue/org_cascade_runs listings, business_plan._load — still use load_json_tolerant or a bare json.loads with a fallback: honest as readers (they never write back) but a listing over an unreadable store shows fewer rows without saying so. Fix: give each listing an 'unavailable' answer via read_json_strict and delete load_json_tolerant when no caller remains.
items.because_means: the work was performed and its answer is NOT ASSESSABLE, with a basis
items.close_note: RESOLVED AS A RECORDED RETENTION, which cluster (a)'s bar explicitly permits: an artefact is either deleted OR kept with a stated reason and a reader that uses it. Every writer is strict (W472) and W506 delivered the rest of this row's substance by making the loader non-silent. Deleting it now would make nothing more honest: its purpose is that a corrupt cache must not take a live subsystem down (ai/memory.py, W241), and its twelve readers are read-only summaries and listings that never write back - removing it would convert each from 'degrades and says so' into a failure, a behaviour change nobody asked for. The decision and its reason are now stated in the function itself. WHAT REMAINS IS NOT ABOUT THIS FUNCTION: four readers carry the reason in their answers and the rest only log it, so a listing over an unreadable store still shows fewer rows without saying so. That is FU-298, whose own why-field records that W506 delivered FU-075's substance, and it belongs where the property lives - P2.18 clause (a), an absence reaches the reader.

items.title: pqc_hardening.py stamps a SHA3 digest with a fixed built-in key as a 'Dilithium5 signature' — relabel or retire
items.why: agentic_core/security/pqc_hardening.py is not a post-quantum scheme; gaas.py and qep_flagship.py record its output as pqc_signature, which reads as cryptographic assurance the code does not give. Retire the field or name it a content hash.

items.title: The ontology engine serves empty graphs and the one real ontology (Law, under knowledge/) is unwired
items.why: agentic_core/reactor/domains/ontology_engine.py reads agentic_core/data/ontologies/ which holds nothing, reached from the domain weaver (a v138 CEO tool) — every domain query answers an empty graph; knowledge/Law/EmploymentTribunal/ontology/*.json is never loaded. Wire the Law graph or retire the engine (audit-before-wire).
items.slot_source: Owner ruling 2026-09-30 ungated it — retire the engine, keep the asset, reclassify it honestly — which is cluster (a)'s own subject: dead code retired or owned. W535 had moved it out only because it sat at OWNER
items.because_means: the work this row asked for was done in this round, not found already done
items.close_note: The Owner RULED on 2026-09-30: retire the engine, keep the asset, reclassify it honestly. Executed, and the ruling's measurement RE-TAKEN rather than trusted: uk_employment_law_v9.json holds 494 concepts and 4 rules with NO relations key at all, and unified_assimilated_graph.json holds 293 nodes that are FILE PATHS with hashes and NO edges key. So the engine served graphs and no graph exists; wiring it would have meant inventing relations. REACHABILITY ESTABLISHED BEFORE REMOVAL, as cluster (a) requires: exactly one live path reached it - v138/ceo.py dispatches the AI CEO's domain_weaver tool into weaver.py, which called ontology_engine.searched(). A repo-wide search found no other importer outside _archive and the register. ontology_engine.py is deleted; the weaver now states that no ontology service exists rather than reporting an absence per domain six times, and names the kept asset. The stale MANDATES.md row that described the engine's behaviour is corrected to RETIRED.

items.title: geospheric/resilience.py ('LSTM' self-healing) is unwired dead code
items.why: agentic_core/biomimicry/geospheric/resilience.py holds a hand-rolled 'LSTM' over a JSON model file; nothing imports it. The organism's real self-healing is agentic_core/organism/self_healing.py. Retire it or wire it honestly (audit-before-wire).

items.title: chroma_db: the legacy vector store above the repository was not relocated (both copies populated)
items.why: scripts/relocate_data_store.py refuses to merge two populated directories; the Owner's <repo-parent>/data/chroma_db and the repo's data/chroma_db both hold data. The Owner decides which is live; the script copies nothing until then.

items.title: v4 R1.0: the halal screen fails a subject that AVOIDS a haram term (negation-blind regex) and seals the FAIL into deliverables and exports
items.why: POST /api/v1/compliance/check on 'a savings app that avoids riba' answers sharia_halal fail 'Prohibited element: riba'; the deliverable is sealed compliance:fail, routed to Change Control, exported with a FAIL banner. Return 'review' with a reason that says the screen cannot tell offered from avoided; reword 'Prohibited element' to 'haram term present'.

items.title: v4 R1.1: the floor-served tafsir body repeats the sourced Arabic CUT MID-WORD under the label 'THE AUTHENTIC ARABIC TEXT'
items.why: engine._subject() cuts the prompt subject at 220 chars with no marker; religion.quran_tafsir puts the sourced Arabic inside that subject, so the study-notes body (rendered, copied, exported, saved to My Work) shows a mutilated ayah labelled authentic. Keep the Arabic out of the floor-visible subject (arabic_text already carries it whole) or never cut inside Arabic.

items.title: v4 R1.2: the Management Systems QMS generator mixes another organisation's recalled text into the document and carries no provenance
items.why: POST /api/v1/mgmt/qms/generate for 'Zed Bakery' returned 'Quality measure for beekeepers yorkshire' (native memory recall mined by the floor) under a green 'Framework Generated' with a download and no ai_provenance/floor_note/QMS record. Generate with ai_text(augment=False), return provenance and a floor note, run assure_delivery.

items.title: v4 R2.0: establishment tells the founder the organism is tending the enterprise while the heartbeat's economy lever is OFF by default
items.why: Every establish/journey answer says, in the present tense, that the living roster tends the new VSB; heartbeat.auto_economy is off unless the Owner enables Self-run, so only the birth cycle ever runs and nothing at the Genesis surface says so. Read the lever at establishment and say 'autonomous cycles OFF — enable Self-run on the Heartbeat page' (also on GET /economy/living-vsbs).

items.title: v4 R2.1: the shipped repository's QMS gate cannot fail on the non-floor path — generator headings and README boilerplate satisfy it
items.why: For an entity whose provenance is not the floor the vsb_repo gate measures the generator's own headings; an enterprise established with no concept/design/commercialisation ships a BUSINESS_PLAN.md that passes. Measure the repo/webapp/mobile gates against the entity's OWN body, or pass served_by='template' for generator-composed documents so the gate records 'not assessable'.

items.title: v4 R3.0: the CEO chat 'meeting' path counts floor echoes as officers' stances
items.why: A message containing 'meeting' runs call_meeting(): six officers are prompted on the floor, the floor echoes the instruction sentence, and the stance detector reads APPROVE/OBJECT/ABSTAIN out of that echo — a deliberation that never happened is minuted. Record no stance when served_by is native; take a stance only from the reply's last line; stamp served_by on every officer entry.

items.title: v4 R3.1: the floor's '_Acting as: <role>_' line names the PREVIOUS call's persona when the prompt was memory-augmented
items.why: gateway.query_meta(augment=True) prepends recall lines holding prior prompts; engine._role() takes the FIRST 'You are the X' in the augmented text, so Board directives, cascades and CCA reviews are labelled with another tier's role. Neutralise persona tokens inside recall lines or make _role() read only the text after the final User: marker.

items.title: v4 R3.4: the Board page presents the Chief as the founder's digital twin while no twin model exists (0 models) and spawned Chiefs are 'Digital Twin of default'
items.why: What serves the Chief is a constant charter sentence plus the last five stored instructions on the floor; /api/v1/twin/models holds 0 models. Say so under the Board header (planned P3.4) and title per-VSB Chiefs by the real owner name or 'the founder', never 'default'.

items.title: v4 R4.0: three Command Center channels (avatar, predictive, spatio) still render invented readings — 'WebRTC stream synchronized · Latency 18ms', a 1.2s 'Calibrated'
items.why: String constants and a setTimeout present measurements nothing takes (W473 fixed the sibling three). Replace with 'not measured — nothing streams here' copy or retire the tiles; 'Calibrate Voice' must say nothing was calibrated.

items.title: v4 R4.1: the native workflow tree returns decision 'proceed' (consistency 1.0, utility 0.85) on a run whose QMS gate was not assessable
items.why: POST /api/v1/native-ai/tree on the floor answers qms_passed=null with basis 'not assessable' yet feeds the un-assessable proxy into the utility and votes proceed. When qms_passed is None the decision and consensus must be 'not assessable' (or abstain) and the chips grey with the basis.

items.title: v4 R4.2: the Resource Fabric marks a composition 'commit-ready' when its gate could not assess (None counted as ready)
items.why: compose/simulate and compositions/run compute commit_ready as 'qms_gate_passed is not False', so a template-served, not_assessable run is commit_ready:true. Make commit_ready tri-state and render null as 'gate could not assess — commit at your judgement'; keep quality_warning on floor-only runs.

items.title: v4 R5.0: the marketplace counts 'enterprise-file-hub' as live over a route that does not exist
items.why: GET /api/v1/catalog/products counts 5 live; enterprise-file-hub→/text-index has no <Route> in App.tsx. Drop it from ROUTE_OVERRIDES (status falls to 'source') and guard that every override route matches a <Route path> in App.tsx (test_w470 checks counts, not route existence).

items.title: v4 R6.0: the Transformation page reports 'Vision Realisation 1.0 — 11/11 pillars realised' from router-mount and non-None checks that cannot fail
items.why: GET /api/v1/transformation/realisation scores every pillar by _has(routes, prefix) or a count/non-None test; the figure and the Heartbeat tab's % read as delivery. Rename it to what it measures (API surface coverage) or derive realisation from /api/v1/plan/state; drop the 'Organism systems healthy' check.

items.title: v4 R6.1: a cycle's declared costs are posted to reserve_fund, so the CFO statements show no operating cost and an inflated reserve
items.why: POST /api/v1/economy/cycle {revenue 1000, costs 200} posts Dr reserve_fund / Cr cash for the costs (metabolism.py reserves = costs + revenue×rate); the P&L shows no expense and the balance sheet a reserve that includes spent money. Post costs as Dr operating_costs / Cr cash, or label the account reserves_and_costs and subtract costs in the P&L.

items.title: v5 R1.0: §11 live compliance (ethical engine) → §10 'safe' / deliverable… — The 'ethical engine' is a bare-word regex (agentic_core/compliance/ethical_engine.py:25-27 _HARM_SEVERE =…
items.why: The 'ethical engine' is a bare-word regex (agentic_core/compliance/ethical_engine.py:25-27 _HARM_SEVERE = kill|murder|...|suicide). Any subject that contains one of those words gets 'human: fail — Severe human-harm indicator', which makes the overall verdict FAIL, even when the subject is a helpful service. The FAIL is then stamped as a real safety judgement: §10 'safe' is recorded met=False, measured=True, source=gate. On material labels the delivery is routed to Change Control (Change Control Agency, CCA) as a compliance violation, and the export's page one reads 'NOT cleared for use'. FIX (the assessor's proposal, a lead): A single harm-vocabulary hit should give 'review' with the matched term named, never 'fail'. Only an ethical row whose coverage is 'engine' should set §10 'safe' as measured. Keyword-only safety evidence should be recorded as source 'screen' with met=None. [docs/VISION_FIDELITY_LEDGER.md v5 R1.0, standing STUB, refutation survived]

items.title: v5 R1.1: §10 bar 'compliant' + 'safe' recorded as MEASURED from keyword… — quality.py:142-146 records 'compliant' as met = (overall != 'fail') and 'safe' as met = no fail among…
items.why: quality.py:142-146 records 'compliant' as met = (overall != 'fail') and 'safe' as met = no fail among ethical/ehs/sharia_halal, both with measured=True and source 'gate'. The inputs are keyword screens that describe themselves as 'not an EHS assessment' and 'not a certification'. The Sharia row passes whenever the word 'halal', 'waqf' or similar appears in the text. assure_delivery (quality.py:228) copies only overall/compliant/verdicts and drops the screen's coverage_gaps and basis. The Deliverables page therefore shows an emerald 'COMPLIANCE: PASS' chip with no 'screen' qualifier (Deliverables.tsx:254-258), and its tooltip says 'MEASURED by this gate: compliant · safe'… FIX (the assessor's proposal, a lead): Record compliant/safe as met=None (basis 'keyword screen only') unless a row with coverage 'engine' actually read the subject. Carry coverage_gaps and basis into quality['compliance'] and label the chip 'screen: pass'. The halal row should not pass on the subject's own use of the word 'halal'. [docs/VISION_FIDELITY_LEDGER.md v5 R1.1, standing STUB, refutation survived]

items.title: v5 R1.2: §11.2 faith-content constitution — sourced-only, exactly (QEP… — The quran-uthmani edition prepends the Basmala to ayah 1 of every surah except 1 and 9. The platform passes…
items.why: The quran-uthmani edition prepends the Basmala to ayah 1 of every surah except 1 and 9. The platform passes this through unmodified (religious_domain/api.py:249-262 fetch_ayah_arabic, :318-324 get_surah, :366-373 get_ayah) and labels it 'Authentic Arabic text… not AI-generated'. As a result, 112 surahs show a first ayah that is not the text of that ayah under Hafs numbering. It also breaks written recall. Ayah 1:1 carries a leading U+FEFF (BOM) as well. FIX (the assessor's proposal, a lead): For surahs other than 1 and 9, strip the leading Basmala from ayah 1 (or request an edition that does not prepend it) and strip U+FEFF. Show the Basmala separately as a header labelled 'not part of ayah 1'. Add a test for 112:1, 2:1 and 1:1. [docs/VISION_FIDELITY_LEDGER.md v5 R1.2, standing PARTIAL, refutation survived]

items.title: v5 R1.3: §10 'modelled · simulated · optimised · ranked' — Genesis stage 5… — genesis.py:394 `winner = (_eligible or candidates)[0]`: when every candidate is vetoed, a vetoed candidate…
items.why: genesis.py:394 `winner = (_eligible or candidates)[0]`: when every candidate is vetoed, a vetoed candidate still wins. The page shows no veto indicator. FIX (the assessor's proposal, a lead): When every candidate is vetoed, stop the journey after stage 5 with status 'blocked_by_screen' and name the vetoes. items.title: v5 R2.0: §4.2 Understand & Map / §4.1 (Genesis Phase 1) — POST /api/v1/genesis/journey {problem:'I keep bees in Yorkshire and varroa mites are killing a third of my…
items.why: POST /api/v1/genesis/journey {problem:'I keep bees in Yorkshire and varroa mites are killing a third of my colonies…', domain:'agriculture', establish:true}. phase_1_conceptualisation.cognitive_cascade contains 0 of the 17 content words in the problem. When floor-served, render these two sections as 'pending the owned model' as the VSB body does, and count them in served_by. items.note: W496 measured it live before building: already delivered by earlier rounds. items.title: v5 R2.1: §4.5 / §4.8 / §11 as it drives the lifecycle — The same beekeeper journey: every candidate gets screen.overall=fail with ethical 'human: fail; ……
items.why: The same beekeeper journey: every candidate gets screen.overall=fail with ethical 'human: fail; … (engine-backed)'. stage_5.vetoed=[pragmatic, innovative, lean]. established_vsb.birth_vitals.first_cycle.held='compliance_fail_hold'. Control, POST /api/v1/compliance/check: {subject:'I keep bees … varroa mites are killing a third of my colonies…'} gives overall fail, but {subject:'An affordable organic varroa treatment service for small-scale… FIX (the assessor's proposal, a lead): Carry the matched term into the surfaced reason. items.title: v5 R2.2: §4.8 Establish / §4.10 Run forever (status, progress map, stage rail) — Every establish path writes status:'operational', stage:'commercialise' as literals, whatever the state. For…

items.title: v5 R3.3: §5 org cascade → §10 quality bar (compliant / safe criteria) — The §10 bar records 'compliant' and 'safe' as MET and MEASURED by the gate whenever no §11 screen says…

items.title: v5 R6.1: §8 survival instinct / §8→§12 economic survival instinct / metabolic… — The ATP 'metabolic energy' behind every survival-instinct lever can only go up. ATPSimulator starts at ratio…
items.why: The ATP 'metabolic energy' behind every survival-instinct lever can only go up. ATPSimulator starts at ratio 5.0 (0.333 normalised). Each update adds production 0.5*efficiency (0.4–0.5) and subtracts consumption 0.1*load (at most 0.1). Every organism_context() read advances it, at most once a second, with load 0.2–1.0. Live, it rose with page polls: 0.396 → 0.456 → 0.831 → 1.0 within about 10 minutes of boot, and stayed at 1.0. So the following can never fire: the economy's reserve raise at atp < 0.3 (metabolism.py:158-163), the heartbeat's self_recovery at < 0.3 (heartbeat.py:194-203), native homeostasis 'protected' at < 0.3, and metabolic_throttle at < 0.2 (heartbeat.py:327). The number… FIX (the assessor's proposal, a lead): Either drive ATP from a real load signal that can fall (request rate, model-call latency or failures), or relabel metabolic energy as a simulation on every surface. Also state that the survival-instinct levers are inert until then. [docs/VISION_FIDELITY_LEDGER.md v5 R6.1, standing STUB, refutation survived]

items.note: REFUTED W519 by three measurements, not abandoned. (1) THE COUNT IS WRONG: 150 orphan .pyc, not 524 - a figure recorded without its method drifts (M-HAND-02). (2) NOT ONE IS TRACKED: git ls-files '*.pyc' returns 0, so none is in the repository and deleting them changes nothing for the repo or for CI. (3) NONE IS IMPORTABLE: all 150 sit inside __pycache__ and ZERO sit outside it, and in Python 3 a __pycache__ entry is only used when its source exists - the cache is validated against the source. So the row's real worry, a stale module being importable beside an archived or deleted source, CANNOT happen. This is untracked local build litter, not a repository defect. Reopen only with an orphan .pyc found OUTSIDE __pycache__, which is the legacy layout that would actually be importable.

items.title: §4.5 candidate ranking is form-only again, and form saturates so candidates tie
items.why: With no §11 framework able to assess a candidate (see the row above), _screen_candidate returns compliance=None and safety=None for every candidate, so stage 5 ranks on form alone. W419 existed because form SATURATES — specificity is min(1, len/2800), so any candidate past ~2800 characters scores exactly 1.000 and all three tie, with the stable sort handing the win to whichever was named first. W483 makes the payload say so (weights_applied {form: 1.0}, the tie is detected and disclosed) instead of advertising weights it never applied, but the RANKING is back to where W419 found it. FIX: an instrument that can separate candidates — or select by an explicit rule and say that is what happened.

items.title: The 46-minute suite is the round's biggest cost, and xdist has never been tried against the shared-store risk
items.why: W487 measured it: integration_tests/ is 46 min over 392 tests (mean 7.1s; top forty = 69%; slowest 134s), and a round runs it once or twice. That is the single largest component of a round's wall clock. pytest-xdist could cut it 3-4x, but this repo's shared stores are exactly what makes it dangerous: [[reference-test-data-isolation-and-concurrency-corruption]] records ~40 false failures from two suites sharing memory.json and the UEG ledgers. If any test cannot be isolated, mark it serial rather than weakening it.

items.title: A stored VSB with no recorded legal form now refuses its economy (422) — nothing migrates the ones already stored
items.why: W488 closed a real hole: _resolve_entity_type's vsb-store leg read a top-level 'entity_type' key NO WRITER SETS (the writer records economy.entity_type), so for any VSB known to the vsb store but not the living roster the caller's CLAIM silently became the binding and W313 evaporated. The fix reads the real key and refuses (422) when a stored entity records no form at all — correct, because a claim must not become the binding. But that refusal is now REACHABLE by any VSB stored before the economy block existed: its owner gets a 422 on /economy/status, /waterfall, /cycle, /close-period and /board-pack with no way forward from the page. Needed: a one-pass audit of the stored VSBs for a missing form, a backfill from the living roster where one exists, and a page route that lets the Owner register the form for the rest (the 422 names the entity-types list but no UI reaches it).

items.title: The avatar is the one caller that keeps cross-request recall — its tenant scoping is asserted in a comment, not by an executing leg
items.why: W488 set augment=False on every generation-class query_meta caller in the repo and left exactly one deliberate exception: the avatar conversation (agentic_core/avatars/api.py), where recall is the point and W333 scopes it to owner_id. The exception is documented in place and a guard leg asserts the comment and the augment=True is there — but NOTHING executes the claim the comment makes: that an authenticated caller reaches only their own namespace plus platform memory, and an UNAUTHENTICATED caller (owner_id None) reaches platform memory only, never another tenant's. That is the one place in the repo where a cross-tenant leak would now be invisible, so it is the one place that needs a behavioural leg: seed two tenants' memories, ask the avatar as each, and prove neither sees the other's.

items.title: A round runs the full suite twice when once would do — the pre-refutation run is wasted whenever the refutation finds anything
items.why: W488 measured a round's wall clock: the full suite is 41 min on an idle machine (258 tests in 26.0 min = 9.9/min), 91.5 min when overlapped with the refutation's 34 agents; the blind sweep is 22.5 min (37.5s per blind, mostly app boot); the refutation workflow is 84.7 min. B2 permits the suite 'twice at most per round' and W488 used both: once before the refutation and once on its fixes. The first run is dead weight whenever the refutation finds real work — W488's found 25 verified findings, so every line of that 41 min was spent on a tree that was about to change. FIX: run the AFFECTED SLICE (-k) during iteration and the full suite ONCE, on the tree that follows the refutation fixes. Keep the second run only when the refutation returns nothing. Worth 41 min per round at no cost and no new machinery; amend B2 in the delivery prompt when done.

items.title: The blind sweep is serial only because blinds mutate one tree — one worktree per blind would cut it from 22.5 min to about 7
items.why: W488 measured 36 blinds in 22.5 min (37.5s each), and most of each blind is app boot, not the assertion. Blinds cannot run in parallel IN ONE TREE because each mutates the repo and byte-restores it; they can run one-per-git-worktree, which is the pattern the refutation workflow already uses safely here (isolation: 'worktree', its own DATA_DIR per worker). FIX: extend the mk_break harness so the blind list is sharded across N worktrees (N = cpu_count - 2, measured 8 CPUs so 6), each with DATA_DIR/WORKSTATION_DATA_DIR/WORKSTATION_UEG_PATH/PROJECTS_DIR of its own, results merged, and the SAME preflight (every anchor matches exactly once) run in each shard before any mutation. Keep the contamination check: the harness must still verify the WATCHed docs are byte-identical after every blind. Expect 3-4x not 6x (8 CPUs, pytest is CPU-bound) — about 15 min per round. Verify by running the same blind set serially and sharded and comparing the caught/vacuous sets exactly, the same discipline FU-249 requires of xdist. FILES CORRECTED W536: this cited scripts/followups.py, which has nothing to do with a blind harness. Its deliverable is a NEW file under scripts/, which the register will not let a row name: check() refuses a row citing a path absent from the working tree, and that rule is correct because it keeps a row checkable. So the row names where its evidence lives TODAY - the document carrying bar (b) and the before-figure, and the conftest whose per-worker isolation any sharding depends on. P2.17's bar (b) asks for the harness's runtime measured before and after, and the W488 before-figure was taken against an ad-hoc script that was never committed, so there is nothing to compare against until this file lands. Note the consequence for the round-start check: a row naming a file that does not exist can never be matched against a change, which is exactly the width FU-345 made countable.

items.close_note: Sharding built and measured, and THE ROW'S PREMISE IS REFUTED. It said the sweep is serial only because blinds mutate one tree, and one worktree per blind would cut 22.5 min to about 7. MEASURED on a real ten-blind list with IDENTICAL verdicts every time: serial 259s wall/259s summed; 2 shards 162s/304s - THE OPTIMUM at 1.60x; 4 shards 211s/508s - WORSE than two. The copy is not the cost (5,126 files in 8s); CONTENTION is, on 6 physical cores and 8.3 GB, because each blind is a whole pytest boot. THE SINGLE TREE WAS NEVER THE LIMIT and 3.2x is unavailable here at any shard count. Built as a COPY rather than a git worktree: a worktree is a clean checkout at a commit while a blind's subject is the round's UNCOMMITTED work, and re-dirtying one does not fail loudly - it yields confident verdicts about code nobody is committing. The sharded path never mutates the real tree and checks its sha to prove it. Serial stays the default and the trusted path.

items.title: Batches are scoped to the gate item, which throws away two thirds of each round's reach — the same mechanism closes three times as many rows swept repo-wide
items.why: The batch mechanism (W487) is being called as 'batches --item P1.18', and that scoping is costing rows for nothing. The generated figures for the SAME class, the SAME mechanism and the SAME files: C3 (invented or constant readings) closes 4 rows inside P1.18, and 12 rows across all items (47 files, advancing 5 more, spanning P1.18, P2.4, P2.8 and P2.9). A class is one rule swept across every file that consumes it; stopping the sweep at the gate item's file list leaves the other consumers emitting the defect the round just proved wrong, and guarantees a later round re-reads the same mechanism. FIX: take the class repo-wide by default and report the closure per item, so the gate's rows still close on schedule while the rest close for free; keep the item filter for the case where a class genuinely spans two unrelated mechanisms. Measured effect on the whole backlog: 173 open rows at 4.0/round is about 44 rounds; at C3's cross-item spread it is roughly half that. Note the optimistic end honestly — C3 is the LARGEST batch, and C7/C1 are smaller.
items.source: W488 forecast/batches reading while reporting the timeline
items.note: Re-registered as FU-255 at its true severity. Marked high for emphasis, which routed it onto P1.18 — 'high severity rides the next open plan item' — and P1.18 is the reached-surface TRUTH gate. A planning-efficiency change costs rounds; it does not make the system say anything untrue, so it does not belong on that gate and must not inflate its count.

items.title: Batches are scoped to the gate item, which throws away two thirds of each round's reach — the same mechanism closes three times as many rows swept repo-wide
items.why: The batch mechanism (W487) is being called as 'batches --item P1.18', and that scoping costs rows for nothing. The generated figures for the SAME class, the SAME mechanism and the SAME files: C3 (invented or constant readings) closes 4 rows inside P1.18, and 12 rows across all items (47 files, advancing 5 more, spanning P1.18, P2.4, P2.8 and P2.9). A class is one rule swept across every file that consumes it; stopping the sweep at the gate item's file list leaves the other consumers emitting the defect the round just proved wrong, and guarantees a later round re-reads the same mechanism. FIX: take the class repo-wide by default and report the closure per item, so the gate's rows still close on schedule while the rest close for free; keep the item filter for the case where a class genuinely spans two unrelated mechanisms. Measured effect on the whole backlog: 173 open rows at 4.0/round is about 44 rounds; at C3's cross-item spread roughly half that. State the optimistic end honestly — C3 is the LARGEST batch; C7 and C1 are smaller. (Re-registered from FU-254, which was marked high for emphasis and routed onto the P1.18 truth gate where a planning-efficiency row does not belong.)
items.source: W488 forecast/batches reading while reporting the timeline

items.title: The 29 generation callers that carried cross-request recall were never probed for what the recall was doing to their output
items.why: W489 flipped the gateway's augment default to False after finding that query/stream/stream_meta still inherited True — 29 generation-class callers, including the live nine-stage synthesis cascade, the CEO blueprint and the digital-twin modeller, had another request's content prepended and presented as analysis of their own subject. The flip stops it happening again, but nothing establishes what it was doing while it happened: no stored output is marked as possibly contaminated, and the memory pool those calls WROTE (gateway logs every interaction) still holds the blended text, so a future recall-enabled caller can retrieve it. FIX: (a) sample the persisted outputs of those 29 surfaces for text that plainly came from another request (the native floor's tell is a Domain: or Problem: label whose value belongs to a different subject) and count how many are affected; (b) decide with the Owner whether contaminated stored outputs are relabelled, regenerated or left with a disclosure; (c) check whether memory rows written from augmented prompts should be marked so recall never re-serves a blend as one tenant's own.

items.title: The six cognitive engines still return fixed markers — W489 made the surfaces honest about it, the engines themselves are P3.12's work
items.why: W489 corrected every surface that claimed nine engines or presented their literals as analysis: the cascade now reports six, says they do not compute, and marks the three meta engines as PLANNED under P3.13. That closes the TRUTH row (FU-146). It does not make the engines work: inkashaf still returns {'status':'SUCCESS','insight':'revealed'}, aqal 'computed', iman alignment 0.99, and MJM re-runs the same six and returns 'optimised' with compliance 1.0 — all persisted into the VSB entity and its genome on every spawn. items.title: Most AI calls do not thread the account id, so their prompts and answers land in the SHARED memory namespace that the two recall surfaces read for every user
items.why: W490 set out to correct a false privacy line and found the claim under it is false too. memory.add_memory stamps owner_id or PLATFORM_NS (agentic_core/ai/memory.py:86) and gateway.query_meta/stream_meta write EVERY completion into it (gateway.py ~195 and ~340). Only a handful of the ~57 gateway call sites in agentic_core pass owner_id at all: board directives, VSB board packs, business-plan text, capital-fund analysis, forge stages, studio stages and the QEP surfaces all omit it, so their prompts AND answers land in the shared platform namespace. query_memory's allow-set is {owner_id or PLATFORM, PLATFORM} (memory.py:112), so the two surfaces that still use recall — the avatar and the AI-CEO chat — can retrieve platform-namespace content that belonged to a DIFFERENT user. W489 removed recall from generation, which closes the biggest consumer, but the WRITES continue and the two conversational readers remain. The Settings page now warns the user plainly rather than claiming their interactions are stored under their account. FIX: thread the authenticated owner_id through every gateway call that has one (a request-scoped default would be better than 57 edits — the same lesson as W489's augment default), and make a write with NO id an explicit decision rather than a fallback; then the warning can come down. Note for whoever takes it: decide with the Owner what happens to the rows already written to the shared namespace.
items.note: W496 closed the LEAK at the mechanism rather than at 52 call sites: a completion written with no account id lands in an UNATTRIBUTED namespace that recall never reads, for any account. Driven: tenant-a, tenant-b and an anonymous caller each recall nothing from it; a deliberate platform note stays recallable; each tenant still recalls its own; and the LEGACY shape (a gateway-written row stamped 'platform' with an agent) is excluded too, so yesterday's writes are not readable by every tenant either. The Settings page now states what is true instead of warning that anything typed may be visible. The remaining work - threading owner_id through the nine user-facing files so a user's own output is recallable BY THEM - is an enhancement, registered separately on P2.4.

items.title: A refutation round can exhaust the disk and lose most of its agents silently — 27 of 45 died creating worktrees, and the run still reported a result
items.why: W490's refutation raised 40 findings and verified only 13: the other 27 agents failed with 'No space left on device' while creating their git worktrees, and the workflow still returned a normal-looking {confirmed: [...]} result. Free space had fallen to about 9 MB. The cause is accumulated worktrees: 56 existed, one per refuter agent across every round since W479, each a full checkout of this repo, and nothing removed them when a round finished. Removing all 55 secondary worktrees recovered 9.6 GB. Two things to fix, neither of them large: (a) the round rhythm must CHECK free space before launching a refutation and REMOVE the round's worktrees after it (git worktree list --porcelain | git worktree remove --force), so the cost does not accumulate; (b) a refutation whose agents died must not read as a completed refutation — the count of agents that errored is in the tool result and should be checked against the count launched before any finding list is trusted. Until (b) exists, read the agent error count by hand every time. Worth considering: the verify agents are read-only (they read code and run pytest against an isolated DATA_DIR) and may not need a worktree at all, which would cut the disk cost by roughly the number of findings.
items.source: W490 refutation (the run itself failed part-way)

items.close_note: Both fixes the row named are built as scripts/refutation_gate.py and the round rhythm now names it. (a) 'before --agents N' REFUSES when the disk cannot hold them, on the MEASURED cost of a checkout (160 MB over 5,126 files, W569) plus headroom, and 'cleanup' removes every secondary worktree and never the main one. (b) 'after --result' reconciles and refuses to call a starved run complete. AND THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS BETTER THAN IT KNEW: it said the errored count is in the tool result; measured, the task NOTIFICATION carries aggregate counts while the RESULT FILE carries one workflow_agent record per agent with its own state and a label naming its lens - so completeness is decided PER LENS from the artefact a round keeps, and a lens that lost every agent is NAMED. W490's failure was that the total looked plausible. Driven on W490's own shape (45 launched, 18 done, 27 errored -> INCOMPLETE), on a dead lens, on a missing record, and on an unrecognised state, which counts as not-done because the failure states cannot be enumerated from a successful run. Also retroactively verified tonight's own refutation: 5 lenses, 35 agents, all done, so its 30 findings were the complete set. Live state measured first: 1 worktree and 23 GB free, so the symptom was absent and only the mechanism was missing.

items.title: No surface calls the evolution apply endpoint, so an approved evolution can only be applied by API

The cause is that no page calls POST /api/v1/vsb/{id}/evolution/apply at all: the cockpit files proposals (Evolve) and the Owner approves the change record in Change Control, but nothing in the UI then applies it, so the genome mutation depends on an API call the Owner cannot make from the product. Either add an Apply control where the approval is visible (Change Control or the cockpit), or have the approval path itself trigger the apply and report generation_advanced.

items.title: An entity's evolution lifecycle reaches no surface: the cycle stamp, the applied stamp and the apply's own outcome are produced and rendered nowhere
items.why: W493's pre-flight keys check names three fields that no page reads. agentic_core/api/vsb.py writes last_evolution_cycle (when a cycle RAN) and last_evolved (when a mutation actually LANDED); no frontend file mentions either, so a user who files ten cycles sees no record that anything happened, and an entity that has never applied a mutation shows nothing distinguishing it from one evolving every day. apply_approved_evolution returns generation_advanced and generation_basis, and no frontend file calls POST /{vsb_id}/evolution/apply at all - the apply is reachable only from the heartbeat (gated on evolution_auto_apply) or a direct API call, so its honest reply about whether the traits changed has no reader. The heartbeat's per-beat record last_vsb_evolved (now carrying the cycle count, the outcome and generation_advanced: False) is published on /api/v1/heartbeat/status and read by no page either. FIX: show the entity's evolution timeline on the cockpit's Organisation or Economy tab - cycles run, last cycle, last APPLIED generation with its date, and whether a review is pending - and give the apply a surface that states generation_basis when an approval is consumed with no applicable mutation. Until then the facts are true and invisible, which is the shape this batch exists to remove.

items.title: OWNER DECISION: is there a constitution document, and what is in it? The endpoint that served one now reports there is none
items.why: W495 (FU-126, S10.3) found /api/v154/constitution/articles fabricating a single article whenever its source file was absent, and the page presenting it as the parsed constitution with three category chips that matched nothing. The file a cleanup moved is _archive/agentic_core/constitution/CONSTITUTION_canonical.md, and I deliberately did NOT restore it: it is the inherited Jules-era v130.0 canon, asserting ~750 articles of live global marketplaces, digitally signed MoUs, ORCID scholar onboarding and post-quantum deployment - none of which exists here. The plan already excludes inherited Jules material as dated and agent-unreliable (answer A.10), so parsing it onto a governance surface would import hundreds of unbuilt capability claims, which is the defect class the truth passes exist to remove. The endpoint therefore reports canon_present:false with a basis, and names what actually governs: the vision doc, the delivery plan and the Owner's rulings, the arms-length CCA, and the gaas.v5 runtime intent gate. THE DECISION THE OWNER OWNS: (a) leave it as it is - the vision plus the rulings plus the CCA ARE the constitution and no separate document should exist; or (b) author a real constitution document for this platform, in which case it should state only what is built or explicitly name what is intended, and this endpoint should parse it; or (c) salvage specific articles from the archived canon that the Owner still stands behind, restated truthfully. Nothing should be restored wholesale. Note: P2.10 (the delivery method held by the arms-length agency) is where a real constitution would most naturally live, since that item already makes Change Control the keeper of what governs.

items.title: OWNER DECISION: the Horizon node/station taxonomy - ratify one, or keep Horizon taxonomy-free
items.why: The Owner's Horizon brief introduces a 0-9 'cosmic blueprint' and 25 'spiritual stations', and has the compressor ASSIGN a station to the user's situation.
