items.title: OWNER DECISION: the hardware ceiling - the roadmap's model stack cannot run on this machine
items.why: Measured on 2026-09-27: this machine has 7.7 GB of RAM total, an Intel i3-1315U (6 cores) and integrated Intel UHD graphics with no CUDA device (nvidia-smi is not installed and no discrete GPU is present). The roadmap's tiers assume otherwise: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B and StarCoder2-15B need roughly 9-12 GB at 4-bit, which is more than the machine's ENTIRE memory, so they cannot load; Llama-3-8B at Q4 is ~4.7 GB, nominally loadable but sharing 7.7 GB with Windows, the browser, the dev server, the backend and the suite, and minutes-per-reply on a CPU-only i3; Qwen-VL vision is out; and 'hot-swap the adapter to save VRAM' has no VRAM to save - Ollama runs on the CPU here. What IS runnable today is llama3.2:1b and llama3.2 (3B), both already pulled, plus the deterministic floor. THE DECISION: (a) design the fabric for a 1-3B local tier plus the floor, and have every higher tier report 'not runnable here' with the measured reason (this is what P3.20 builds by default); (b) provision hardware (a discrete GPU with 12-24 GB, or a rented instance) and state which tiers it unlocks; or (c) route specific high-value tasks to an Owner-gated external accelerant, which the platform supports and keeps off by default. Blocks the inventory half of P3.20. Default if undecided: (a). OWNER DECIDED 2026-10-03: DEFAULT (a), taken explicitly rather than by expiry. Asked to proceed with the agreed sequence, the Owner wrote "the last cognitive item (P3.20, under FU-271 stated default)" - so the fabric is designed for a 1-3B local tier plus the deterministic floor, and every higher tier reports that it is not runnable here with the MEASURED reason. Neither of the other two options is taken: no hardware is provisioned and no Owner-gated external accelerant is enabled. BUILT W559 in agentic_core/ai/native/tiers.py, and the decision is named on the surface (/api/v1/native-ai/tiers reports owner_decision citing FU-271 default (a)) so a later reader can find out whether it still stands rather than inheriting it. THE MACHINE IS MEASURED AT CALL TIME, not recorded: psutil reports 7.69 GB today, which corroborates the 7.7 GB measured on 2026-09-27, and a guard reads the module AST to assert no machine figure is a constant in executable code - because a typed figure is correct the day it is written and is a claim about hardware nobody re-measured on every day after.
items.note: OWNER RULED 2026-09-27: design the fabric for the 1-3B local tier plus the deterministic floor, with every higher tier reporting 'not runnable here' and the measured reason; add an Owner-gated external accelerant for NAMED drafting tasks; defer buying hardware until a specific deliverable measurably fails on 3B. P3.20 makes the hardware a declared fact, so a GPU later lights the tiers up with no code change.

items.title: OWNER DECISION: the tribunal outcome predictor is refused by default - confirm, or name a data source
items.why: The roadmap proposes a Tribunal Outcome Prediction that takes evidence strength, the opponent's likely arguments and 'judge tendencies (from public rulings)' and outputs a probability distribution of winning and a settlement range, labelled a 'Predictive Heuristic'. I have REFUSED it as specified and built the procedural half instead (P3.24 stage 1: deadlines and hearing windows computed from published rules and the case's own dates - checkable arithmetic, labelled a schedule). The reasons: there is no outcome dataset in this repo, no judge data, 'judge tendencies' is neither available nor a proper basis for advice to a party, and a settlement range shown to someone in a live matter is a number they may act on however it is labelled. THE DECISION: (a) confirm the refusal - the platform computes schedules and assembles evidence, and never forecasts an outcome (the default); or (b) name a real data source (e.g. a published outcomes dataset) and accept that any figure would be labelled a heuristic over that source, never a legal opinion, and never shown without its base rate and sample size. Governs the scope of P3.24.
items.note: OWNER RULED 2026-09-27: the tribunal outcome predictor is REFUSED and stays refused. What is built instead: the procedural timeline (deadlines and windows computed from published rules and the case's own dates - a schedule, not a forecast) and an evidence-completeness checklist (what the claim's elements require against what the bundle contains). No probability of a legal outcome, ever.

items.title: The archived nine-engine bootstrap must NOT be recovered as-is: two of its three meta engines return fabricated ratifications and its base class hard-codes confidence 0.95
items.why: The roadmap's Phase 1 says to un-archive cognitive/bootstrap.py and register the nine engines. Measured on 2026-09-27: bootstrap.py exists only at _archive/jules-unwired/agentic_core/cognitive/bootstrap.py and imports the nine from foundational/ and meta/, which in the live tree are EMPTY package shells (__init__.py only) - six engines live at the top level of cognitive/ and the three meta engines do not exist in the live tree at all, though the registry's EngineType enum declares them. The archived meta engines are 7-line stubs returning literals: niyyah_engine returns {'ratified': True, 'signatures': ['council_node_1','council_node_2','council_node_owner'], 'intent_status': 'COMMITTED'} - a fabricated governance record with three invented signatories - and the archived base_engine.py hard-codes confidence=0.95 on every successful output, which is the shape FU-224 and FU-233 already record. FIX (the three engines themselves ride the meta-engine item; this row rides the engine-contract item because that is where cognitive/ routes): write the three engines so each reads its input or returns assessable:false with a reason; recover the CALL CONTRACT from the archive (one signature the engines implement, per FU-221) and nothing else; and never register an engine that cannot compute. Recovering the file without reading it would import a fabricated ratification into the clearance chain P3.14 is meant to make refusable.

items.title: The cognitive engines have no path to a model at all - not a stub call, no import: measured 0 of 6
items.why: Recorded as the measurement behind P3.12, because it is stronger than 'they return constants': a grep for gateway|orchestrator|complete( across all six engine modules returns ZERO for every one of them. There is no disabled call, no try/except around a model, no injection point - the engines were never wired to anything, so making them compute is new wiring rather than repair. The roadmap is right that this is the first job, and its own deliverable is the right shape: one engine reasoning about a real input through a local model, with the result traceable to the call that produced it. Two constraints this repo already knows: on THIS hardware the runnable local tier is llama3.2:1b / 3B (see FU-271), so the not-assessable path will be the common path and must be first-class, not a fallback literal; and the engine must carry what served it, because a reasoning step with no provenance cannot be told from the floor composing headings.
items.slot_source: P3.13's ACCEPT is a disjunction (refuse OR compute) and the meta tier COMPUTES deterministically, so the bar is met without a model. FU-275 is the six foundational engines' missing model path, which is the native AI fabric's work (P3.20's tier registry and router), not this item's.

items.title: 52 of 61 gateway call sites still thread no account id, so their output is unattributed and recallable by nobody - including its own author
items.why: W496 closed the LEAK at the mechanism: a completion written with no account id lands in an UNATTRIBUTED namespace that recall never reads, for any account (driven: tenant-a, tenant-b and an anonymous caller all recall nothing from it, while a deliberate platform note stays recallable and each tenant still recalls its own). That removes the cross-tenant exposure whatever a call site does, which is why it was the right fix rather than editing 52 sites. What remains is the ENHANCEMENT: measured on 2026-09-27, 52 of 61 gateway call sites across 28 files pass no owner_id, so the work those users ask for is stored unattributed and cannot be recalled even BY THEM - the AI CEO chat and the avatar therefore recall far less than the user typed. Nine of the 28 files already have a user in scope (vsb.py 4 calls, synthesis_studio.py 3, change_control.py 3, qep_intelligence.py 2, genesis.py 2, capital_fund.py 2, integration_surface.py 1, projects/api.py 1, organism/reconfiguration.py 1), so threading is plumbing there; the rest (products.py 8, digital_twin.py 3, swarm.py 2, genome.py 1, ...) are platform-internal calls with no user, where unattributed is the correct namespace and nothing needs changing. FIX: thread owner_id through the nine user-facing files and assert per file that a user's own call is recallable BY THAT USER and by nobody else.

items.title: The archived employment-tribunal corpus is 342 rows of 'Simulated content for <filename>' stamped EXTRACTED, and its submission report tells the Owner the evidence is on their side
items.why: The Owner asked whether the archive already holds work on the legal matter. It holds 272 files, and the corpus is SIMULATED. _archive/scripts/Law/EmploymentTribunal/content_extraction.py says so in its own comment - 'Simulated extraction with granular citations / In real execution, pypdf / python-docx would be used' - and then stamps every row status EXTRACTED with granularity page_paragraph and a sha256 computed over the PLACEHOLDER STRING, so the provenance hash attests the placeholder rather than the document. The output, extracted_content_v9.0_gold_exec.json (151 KB, tracked in git), holds 342 rows: all status EXTRACTED, all with text, and 17,265 characters of text in TOTAL - a median of 50 characters per document, every one of the form 'Simulated content for RM CV Science Oct 2025 (1).docx'. source_inventory_v9.0_gold_exec.json and unified_assimilated_graph.json are built on those rows. And _archive/legacy-archive/law-grand-operation/v9.0-ULTIMATE-definitive/FINAL_SUBMISSION_REPORT_v9.0_ULTIMATE.md tells the Owner, about a REAL live tribunal matter: 'Granular Citations: All chronology entries, legal tests, evidentiary references include page/paragraph' and 'You are ready. The evidence is on your side. Proceed with confidence.' That is the most consequential instance of this defect class in the repository: a submission-readiness verdict over placeholders, in a live dispute. WHAT TO DO: (a) do NOT recover the corpus - it contains no document content and its hashes attest nothing; (b) recover only the SHAPE, which is sound (the manifest row schema path/filename/type/status/timestamp/extracted_text/granularity/sha256, and _archive/jules-phase2/.../evidence_ingestion.py's inbox + graph + per-file skeleton, which globs only *.txt and imports a src/organism tree that does not exist here); (c) write a README marker into those archive directories saying the content is simulated, so no later round or agent reads them as prior analysis; (d) when the real extractor is installed (FU-269), re-extract from the Owner's own documents through the explicit inbox (FU-272) with a hash over the REAL bytes. ESCALATED THE SAME DAY, AFTER FOLLOWING THE TRAIL INTO THE LIVE TREE: the simulated corpus did not stay in the archive. products/Law/VSB-SIG-LAW-OMNIOCTO-19.0/outputs/ is a LIVE, git-tracked directory holding five documents built on it, including three READY-TO-SEND EMAILS addressed to the opposing solicitor by name with the respondent's HR in copy, in the Owner's real matter (case number in the subject line). Email_1_Exhibit_Q1_Demand.md asserts in the first person: 'I have reviewed the internal HR performance record ("Exhibit Q-1") which indicates that I maintained a 94% punctuality rate during the monitoring period of October 2025 to January 2026', demands disclosure under Rule 31 within 7 days, references 'the recommendations made by Occupational Health on 14 November 2025', and cites 'the precedent in Thompson v TechFlow Ltd [2026] EAT 12'. That citation propagated through the archived pipeline as a legal_source (jules-phase2 stl_procedural_specs.yaml) and a legal_authority graph node before arriving in a sendable letter - a fabricated authority before a tribunal is among the most damaging things that can happen to a litigant. None of these particulars can have come from a document: the pipeline read 342 placeholder strings. ACTION TAKEN in W496: a VERIFY-BEFORE-USE block prepended to all five live documents naming each particular to check (nothing deleted - they are the Owner's files and the content is evidence of what was generated), and a marker README in the four affected archive directories. ACTION FOR THE OWNER: verify or remove each particular; the structure of these documents is useful, the facts in them are not sourced. THE LESSON FOR THE BUILD: this is why FU-272's inbox is explicit and human-gated and why FU-269 installs a real extractor - a generated legal artefact must cite a page and a line that exist, or it must not be generatable. OWNER RESPONSE 2026-09-27: 'I cannot verify so proceed accordingly.' ACTED ON THE SAME DAY - the particulars were REDACTED out of the live documents rather than left behind a warning: an unverifiable specific in a sendable letter is a risk a banner does not remove. Every occurrence across six live documents was replaced with a marked blank ([[VERIFY-EXHIBIT]], [[VERIFY-FIGURE]], [[VERIFY-PERIOD]], [[VERIFY-DATE]]) and the cited authority was removed outright with a note saying why. The originals are preserved byte-for-byte at products/Law/VSB-SIG-LAW-OMNIOCTO-19.0/outputs/_unverified_originals/ with a README stating they must not be sent - nothing was destroyed, because they are evidence of what was generated. Verified after: 0 live files still assert an unsourced particular, and the templates keep the structure that is genuinely useful (Rule 31 mechanics, ss.15/20/21 framing, the Unless Order escalation). WHAT REMAINS FOR THIS ROW: the same discipline as an ACCEPTANCE BAR on P3.23/P3.24 - a generated legal artefact must cite a page and a line that exist in a document the platform actually read, or it must not be generatable.
items.source: W496 archive audit (the Owner's instruction: search the archive for work already done)
items.note: W496 audited the archive on the Owner's instruction and acted the same day: marker READMEs in the four affected archive directories; the unverifiable particulars REDACTED out of six live documents (exhibit reference, every punctuality figure, monitoring period, OH date) with the cited authority removed outright; the originals preserved byte-for-byte in _unverified_originals/ with a README stating they must not be sent. Verified: 0 live files still assert an unsourced particular, and the templates keep the structure that is useful. The rider - the acceptance bar for any future generated legal artefact - is FU-278 on P3.23.

items.title: ACCEPTANCE BAR for the legal specialist: a generated artefact must cite a page and a line that exist in a document the platform read, or it must not be generatable
items.why: The rider FU-277 leaves behind. W496's archive audit found the previous Law pipeline generating a ready-to-send disclosure letter over 342 rows of 'Simulated content for <filename>': it asserted an exhibit reference, a punctuality figure, a monitoring period, an Occupational Health date and a case citation, none of which existed in anything it read, and the Owner confirmed none could be verified (the particulars were redacted out in W496 and the originals preserved). The lesson is an ACCEPTANCE BAR for P3.23's legal specialist, not a one-off cleanup: (a) every factual particular in a generated artefact carries the document id and the location it came from, and a particular with no location cannot be rendered; (b) a citation of an authority is either resolved against a real source the platform holds or is refused - never emitted as prose; (c) the artefact states, on its face, which of its particulars came from a document and which are blanks the user must fill; (d) a guard drives the empty-corpus case and proves the generator produces a TEMPLATE with blanks rather than a letter with invented specifics. Without this bar the same class returns the first time the specialist runs on a thin bundle.
items.slot_source: rider of FU-277 (W496): an acceptance bar belongs to the item that BUILDS the thing it bars - the legal specialist is P3.23's work, while this row's files route to P2.4 by filename

items.title: W497's guard was green alone and red in the suite: eight test sites asked asyncio for THE event loop, so they asserted what ran before them
items.why: FIXED IN W498 - registered so the class is on the record, not because work remains. asyncio.get_event_loop() raises on 3.12 once any earlier test has created and closed a loop, so test_w497_a_screen_that_matched_nothing_is_not_a_pass passed under -k and failed the full run at 1eb972a0 with RuntimeError: there is no current event loop. CI caught it before I did, because I pushed W497 without checking the run. Eight sites had the shape (lines 1483 1513 1616 1669 20757 21437 21451 21457); _ensure_loop() already existed in the file for exactly this and now serves all of them. test_w498b drives the condition instead of hoping to be scheduled into it - it calls asyncio.run() to unset the loop, re-runs the assertion through the helper, unsets it again, and scans the file for the two dangerous shapes with needles built by concatenation so it cannot match its own source. THE STANDING LESSON: check the CI run of every push before starting the next round, and a guard that reads ambient state is not a guard.
items.source: W498 (the full suite, and CI at 1eb972a0 which I had not checked)

items.title: OWNER DECISION: the plan has no Phase 5 - it ends at the Owner's switches and never reaches commercialisation, which is what the platform is for
items.why: grep for P5 / 'Phase 5' in docs/FABLE_DELIVERY_PROMPT.md returns ZERO hits. The plan runs P1 truth (18/18 done) -> P2 reach (0/16) -> P3 capability (0/25) -> P4 the Owner's switches (0/6), and stops. There is no item for a first paying tenant, a pricing model, support operations, or the entity repository handed over as a versioned product - although the README's first line calls this an AI-mediated workspace for moving ideas 'from concept to commercial output' and the lifecycle is named Concept->Commercialise. Two independent external audits of this repo inferred a commercial destination from that vocabulary and were not wrong to; what they got wrong was the SHAPE (they inferred a multi-tenant SaaS with real-money rails, which the canon rules out: virtual WST, local-first, external providers opt-in). A PROPOSED SKELETON, for the Owner to ratify, reject or replace: P5.1 the first tenant journey end to end on the virtual economy, measured not narrated; P5.2 the price of a VSB stated in WST with the waterfall that produces it (the section 4 waterfall already exists and is Owner-adjustable); P5.3 support operations - who answers when an autonomous entity is wrong, and what the platform records when it does; P5.4 the entity repository as a shippable artifact (docs + site + app + board pack) with a version, a changelog and a handover that does not need this repo; P5.5 what is NOT for sale, stated plainly - the faith content, the Fitrah spectrum, anything real-money. THE DECISION THE OWNER OWNS: (a) ratify a Phase 5 of roughly this shape; (b) rule that commercialisation is out of this plan's scope and belongs to a separate programme, in which case the plan should say so where it currently just stops; or (c) replace the skeleton. Nothing should be built into a phase the Owner has not named.

items.title: ten dependencies are pinned and imported by nothing: five opentelemetry packages, asyncpg, alembic, aiosqlite - the gap is wiring, not procurement
items.why: An external audit named 'no APM, no error tracking' and 'JSON files, no relational DB' as gaps to procure. Measured: opentelemetry-api, -sdk, -proto and two otlp exporters (all 1.40.0), plus asyncpg 0.31.0, alembic 1.18.4 and aiosqlite 0.22.1, are ALL pinned in requirements.txt, and grep over agentic_core, integration_tests and scripts finds NO file importing any of them. So both 'gaps' are adoption gaps. What DOES exist, measured: psutil vitals in 8 modules, 13 record_outcome call sites across 6 modules (the outcome ledger built W495), and the hash-chained UEG log referenced in 11 api modules - so the platform is not blind to itself, it has no EXTERNAL telemetry and no error capture. THE WORK: for the database three, this is P4.4's pre-flight - a migration dry-run and rollback proven on a copy - so they stay pinned and the row rides P4.4. For the five opentelemetry packages there is NO plan item that owns observability at all, which is the finding: either an item is added and they are wired to the outcome ledger and the UEG chain that already exist, or they are retired from the manifest. A dependency pinned for a year and imported by nothing is a claim the manifest makes and the code does not keep.
items.source: W499 (verifying an external audit's scalability and observability gaps)
items.note: PREMISE FALSIFIED by verifying before acting (W500). The row said ten dependencies are pinned and imported by nothing, so the gap is wiring. The measurement 'no file imports them' was right; the INFERENCE was wrong. pip show reports opentelemetry-api and -sdk as Required-by: chromadb, and chromadb is LIVE - agentic_core/ai/ceo/memory_v01.py imports it lazily, and memory_v01 is imported by api/v138/ceo.py and avatars/api.py, the same two recall callers FU-280 is about. asyncpg is Required-by: prefect. requirements.txt is a 298-line lock that CI and the Dockerfile both install from, so it carries transitive dependencies by design: removing one would break the install, not tidy it. items.title: 25 of 43 DECLARED direct dependencies are imported by no .py in the repo — measured with each distribution's own top-level module names, not its package name
items.why: FU-282 was dropped because its transitive-pin premise was false. This is the claim that survives re-measurement, and the instrument matters: a first pass matched the DISTRIBUTION name and reported 28, which was wrong - pyyaml imports as yaml, PyJWT as jwt, scikit-learn as sklearn, psycopg2-binary as psycopg2, pyro-ppl as pyro, z3-solver as z3, POT as ot. Re-run against each installed distribution's own top_level.txt: of 43 direct dependencies in pyproject.toml [tool.poetry.dependencies], 16 are imported and 25 are imported by NO .py under agentic_core, integration_tests or scripts - langchain, langchain-community, streamlit, redis, sqlmodel, sqlalchemy, prefect, transformers, shap, PyJWT, pandas, seaborn, plotly, scikit-learn, pyro-ppl, ray, celery, web3, z3-solver, sympy, qiskit, pennylane, oqs, psycopg2-binary, firebase-admin. TWO ARE UNDECIDABLE and are not counted: POT is not installed here, and autogen's top_level.txt is empty so the instrument could not read its modules - an empty module list makes any() false, which would have reported it as unimported for the wrong reason. WHY THIS IS NOT YET A DELETION LIST: a dependency can be needed without a source import. psycopg2-binary and sqlalchemy/sqlmodel are exactly P4.4's pre-flight material and a driver is loaded by URL, not imported; redis may be reached the same way. So each of the 25 needs one of three verdicts - reached without an import (name the mechanism), held deliberately for a named plan item, or removable - and the ones that are removable matter, because CI and the Dockerfile both install from requirements.txt and the heavy ones here are ray, celery, qiskit, pennylane, transformers, web3 and firebase-admin. NOTHING IS REMOVED UNTIL EACH HAS A VERDICT.
items.source: W500 (re-measuring FU-282's premise with real module names after it was falsified)

items.title: FU-057's remaining half: a gated action that raised is retried OUTSIDE the gate, so a refusal inside the action runs again ungated
items.why: W502 fixed the WORDING half of FU-057 (a reused transfer id means an earlier attempt may have debited, and the header no longer publishes an UNKNOWN as 'false'). The second half of that row is not done and is recorded here rather than left inside a closed one. The claim, unverified so far: the W463 design retries a gated action OUTSIDE the gate's decision, so when the action itself raises after the gate consumed an approval, the retry runs without the gate. What IS measured: _transfer_core consumes the approval at gate time, before the action runs, and _restore_consumed_approval exists precisely because the action may never run - so the pieces are there and the question is whether the retry path re-enters the gate or bypasses it. THE WORK: drive a settlement whose action raises AFTER the materiality gate consumed an Owner approval, then retry it, and assert the retry is inside the gate's decision (a fresh hold or the same approval, never an ungated run). If it turns out the retry is already gated, close this with the measurement that says so - the row's claim would then be the thing that was wrong.
items.source: W502 (found while fixing FU-057: the header override)
items.slot_source: W502: measured while fixing FU-057's wording half; it is the same transfer-answer code path

items.title: FU-058's remaining part: the strict read's retry sleeps block the event loop in async routes
items.why: W502 fixed two of FU-058's three parts - a locked or unwritable store now answers 503 with the ledger_written wording instead of a bare 500, and a raised cycle leaves an economy.cycle_raised record in the chain as the heartbeat path already did. The third part is NOT done and is recorded here rather than left inside a closed row. THE CLAIM: the strict read retries with time.sleep, and in an async route (POST /cycle, /close-period, /transfer are async def) a blocking sleep holds the event loop, so every other request on the worker waits for a contended store. WHAT IS MEASURED SO FAR: the routes are async def and the ledger read retries exist; what has NOT been measured is the sleep duration, how many retries, and whether the loop is actually held for a user-visible time. THE WORK: measure the blocking window first (a contended store, timed), then move the retries off the loop (asyncio.to_thread or a threadpool read) only if the measurement justifies it - and if it does not, close this with the measurement, because a fix nobody needs is still a change to a money-adjacent path.
items.source: W502 (FU-058's third part, left undone deliberately)
items.slot_source: W502: the same /cycle route whose error mapping this round fixed

items.title: Two concurrent visits of one entity leave a row describing one of them and a counter reflecting both
items.why: FU-063's seventh sub-defect, kept separate because it is a concurrency shape rather than the outcome-vocabulary one W503 closed. Measured: living_vsbs._update_entry re-reads the roster under store_lock and mutates only its own entry (W463 sixth refutation), so no OTHER entity's row is lost and operating_cycles cannot drop an increment. But operate_vsb takes no per-entity visit claim, so two visits of ONE entity interleave: visit A may write last_hold while visit B pops it, and the row's final last_hold / last_error / outcome describe whichever finished last while operating_cycles counts both. The money is safe (peek-then-consume means the second visit gets intake_consumed_elsewhere, W466/W467), so this is a REPORTING defect: the row asserts an outcome that was not the outcome of the visit its counter attributes. Fix: claim the entity for the duration of a visit (a nonce like the one W503 gave the evolution apply, FU-019), or record the outcome per visit rather than as a single mutable row.

items.title: P2.17's ACCEPT clause contradicts its own part (a) and cannot be satisfied as written
items.why: Found by auditing item ACCEPT criteria against the tree (the first such audit). P2.17's ACCEPT demands 'a proposal naming two DISJOINT items is produced from the real register and plan, and its disjointness is asserted from the file sets rather than stated'. But part (a) of the SAME item says that framing was 'WRONG in its central idea - corrected W500 after measuring, before any of it was built', because disjointness 'avoids CONFLICT; it throws away the leverage' - rows on the same files share the measurement, the guard, the blinds and the refutation, which is the ~77% of a round that is not the suite. The item was corrected in its body and its acceptance bar was not. As written, P2.17 cannot be closed without building the thing it says is wrong. W501 built the corrected version (a bundle is a file-connected component cut by item). NEEDS AN OWNER RULING or an explicit restatement of the ACCEPT clause to match part (a); a build round must not quietly reinterpret an acceptance bar. Note also that part (b) - the parallel suite, proven to produce the same pass/fail set as the serial one, with a per-worker isolated store - is unbuilt, so P2.17 is not closable on either reading yet.
items.note: re-registered without a slot_source: the register slots owner-gated work to OWNER by its own rule, and slot_source means a deliberate ITEM placement, so the two together make a row the plan-currency guard rightly refuses. Superseded by the re-add; no content changed.

items.title: P2.17's ACCEPT clause contradicts its own part (a) and cannot be satisfied as written
items.why: Found by auditing item ACCEPT criteria against the tree (the first such audit, W504). P2.17's ACCEPT demands 'a proposal naming two DISJOINT items is produced from the real register and plan, and its disjointness is asserted from the file sets rather than stated'. But part (a) of the SAME item says that framing was 'WRONG in its central idea - corrected W500 after measuring, before any of it was built', because disjointness 'avoids CONFLICT; it throws away the leverage' - rows on the same files share the measurement, the guard, the blinds and the refutation, which is the ~77% of a round that is not the suite. The item was corrected in its body and its acceptance bar was not. As written, P2.17 cannot be closed without building the thing it says is wrong. W501 built the corrected version (a bundle is a file-connected component cut by item). NEEDS AN OWNER RULING or an explicit restatement of the ACCEPT clause to match part (a); a build round must not quietly reinterpret an acceptance bar. Note also that part (b) - the parallel suite, proven to produce the same pass/fail set as the serial one, with a per-worker isolated store - is unbuilt, so P2.17 is not closable on either reading yet.

items.title: STAGE 1: 17 of 48 open build items state no ACCEPT bar, so they cannot be closed as written - 12 are also unsized
items.why: The measurement behind W505, and the reason no P2 item had closed while 32 rows closed in six rounds: an item closes on its ACCEPT criteria, and 17 open build items state none. Nothing was forgotten - there was nothing to check them against. MEASURED (scripts/../stage1_audit.py, bodies parsed from each slot heading to the next heading/MILESTONE/SEQUENCING - an earlier count was WRONG because its pattern required a bracket after the slot and so reported ten Horizon and ruling items as having no body at all): of 48 open build items, 31 state a bar and 17 do not. The 17: P2.2, P2.4, P2.7, P2.8, P3.0, P3.1, P3.2, P3.3, P3.4, P3.5, P3.6, P3.7, P3.8, P3.10, P3.11 (P2.3 and P2.5 were in this list and W505 wrote bars for them from their own bodies and closed them). Of the 17, TWELVE also carry no registered row - unbarred AND unsized, so neither population measures them: P3.0, P3.1, P3.2, P3.3, P3.4, P3.5, P3.6, P3.7, P3.8, P3.10, P3.11 plus P2.3 (now closed). THE WORK, and W505 demonstrated it twice: an item whose body already lists its deliverables does not need a bar invented - the deliverables ARE the bar, and writing them as ACCEPT is transcription plus a guard. P2.3 and P2.5 were closed exactly that way. THE RULE this establishes: a round that finishes an item's work must also write its bar if it has none, or the work cannot be recognised. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the plan's own item projection (128 rounds) is an average over a population most of which nobody has measured, and it says so; 26 of 48 build items being unbarred or unsized is that weakness stated in figures. CORRECTED W505 (second pass): the figure 17 is STALE and this row used it in its own reasoning before checking it. Six of the seventeen have since been given a bar or closed - P2.3 and P2.5 were barred and closed, and P2.4, P2.7 and P2.8 were barred in the same round; P2.2 was never unbarred at all, its GUARD sits inline mid-line and the audit's line-start pattern missed it. The remaining unbarred set is P3.0-P3.8, P3.10, P3.11 and P2.16 (FU-297 covers P2.16). A measurement row that OVERSTATES a problem is the same defect as one that understates it.

items.title: Thirteen tolerant readers still LOG rather than surface their store's incompleteness
items.why: W506 delivered FU-075's substance: load_json_tolerant now delegates to the new read_json_reported and LOGS the store, the calling site and exactly what is missing, so a corrupt store is attributable everywhere instead of silent. FOUR readers were fully converted and carry the reason in their own answers - revenue's pending_summary (store_incomplete + counts_are_incomplete), charity's approved signals, the heartbeat's screening rotation, and the avatar's compliance line, which now says a screen is UNKNOWN rather than omitting it. THIRTEEN callers remain on the logging path: ai/native/model_resource.py, api/agent_hub.py, api/board.py (x2), api/capital_fund.py, api/integration_surface.py, api/operational_excellence.py, api/resource_fabric.py, api/swarm.py (x2), api/user_workspace.py, vbs/dcms.py, vbs/qms.py. THE WORK: give each caller the reason in its own response, as the four converted ones do - a log line is a weaker remedy than a field on the answer, because the person reading the number never sees the log. THEN delete load_json_tolerant, which is what the original row asked for and which cannot honestly be done while thirteen callers use it. WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN ONE PASS: each of the thirteen is a different caller shape, and a careless conversion turns a working list endpoint into a 500 or drops a field a page reads; rewriting thirteen heterogeneous sites in one unattended batch is how a round ships a regression it cannot attribute. TRANCHE 1 of 5 DONE (W534): vbs/qms.py - qms.py now loads through read_json_reported, and defect_summary carries store_incomplete plus counts_are_incomplete on the convention economy/revenue.pending_summary set (present only when there IS a reason, so absent means read whole). The rate_basis additionally states WHICH WAY an unreadable store moves the figure: the defects it cannot read are the ones missing from the numerator, so a truncated store makes the non-conformance rate look no worse than the truth and possibly better. Both routes that print those figures disclose it too, and the defects listing carries listing_is_incomplete beside the rows, because a caller rendering a list may never read the summary. TWELVE REMAIN: ai/native/model_resource.py, api/agent_hub.py, api/board.py (x2), api/capital_fund.py, api/integration_surface.py, api/operational_excellence.py, api/resource_fabric.py, api/swarm.py (x2), api/user_workspace.py, vbs/dcms.py. load_json_tolerant cannot be deleted until they are done, which is what FU-075 waits on.

items.title: A framework covered only by a word list appears in neither coverage_gaps nor assessed_by
items.why: _coverage_report (agentic_core/api/compliance.py:197-203) builds coverage_gaps from coverage in ('none','screen') and assessed_by from assessed(), which requires coverage=='engine'. A row with coverage 'vocabulary' and status 'review' therefore lands in NEITHER list. Measured W506: a probe entity screened 5 frameworks; coverage_gaps named 4 and assessed_by named 0, so sharia_halal fell out of the account entirely. A reader taking the two lists as a partition of the frameworks concludes that framework was neither missing nor assessed -- the word-list pass is silently invisible, which is the shortfall the three-state 'compliant' field was added to prevent. The fix must either name a third list or widen coverage_gaps, and coverage_gaps has many readers, so its meaning cannot be changed without grepping them (the W495 lesson).

items.title: OWNER DECISION: close the §12 reinvestment loop by crediting venture investees, or leave positions recorded-unfunded
items.why: W506 took P2.7(7)'s LABEL arm and left the funding arm for the Owner, because funding changes WHERE the economy's virtual money flows and the waterfall's proportions are the Owner's (template-bounded, UEG-logged). THE FACTS. A cycle posts to distribution_user_projects and records positions against named living VSBs; no investee is ever credited (_record_positions_locked writes the investor's holdings only, while transfers.record_transfer beside it does queue the receiver's intake). W446's refuter reproduced it twice: a 21.26 WST position arrived nowhere. As of W506 every figure a reader sees says 'recorded, unfunded' and the wording comes from one server constant, so nothing now overstates it. WHAT FUNDING WOULD TAKE, measured: record_transfer cannot be reused, because the investor's debit has ALREADY happened as the waterfall distribution and a second debit is the W504 'a spend is not a second distribution' defect; it needs a NEW credit-only primitive, idempotent per position, queueing intake only for ids that resolve to a live VSB (positions can name demo candidates, which are not entities and must stay unfunded and labelled). W506 also fixed the precondition: allocate() rounded each share independently so positions did not sum to the budget (100.0 -> 100.01, 33.33 -> 33.32), which would have created and destroyed virtual money the moment anything was funded; the residual now lands on the largest position and the sum is exact. THE DECISION is whether distribution_user_projects is capital that should reach the investee's waterfall (closing §6/§12 as the model describes) or a notional allocation that should stay on the investor's books. Virtual WST either way; no real-money rail is involved.
items.slot_source: OWNER RULING 2026-09-29: close the loop as a user-adjustable share defaulting to the user_projects waterfall proportion already set (0.0 keeps today's recorded-unfunded behaviour). P2.4 owns the economy's flows, handed from P2.9.

items.title: The parallel suite stalls about one run in three, with every worker in flight at once - cause not established
items.why: W507 delivered the per-worker store isolation FU-249 asked for and MEASURED the win: 50m42s serial to 10m35s on six workers (4.8x), with the pass sets matching exactly (466 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed both ways). It is NOT the round default because of this row. MEASURED FAILURE MODE: of six parallel runs, three completed and three STALLED - at 74%, 89% and 57% - and in the stalled runs EVERY worker was in flight simultaneously (a -v run showed six tests started with no verdict, one per worker) with the controller and one worker process still alive and no CPU. So it is a simultaneous stall of all workers, not one slow test. WHAT WAS RULED OUT: (a) store_lock itself - it is a per-path threading.RLock plus an O_CREAT|O_EXCL lockfile with a bounded 10s timeout that RAISES TimeoutError and breaks a stale file after 30s, so it cannot deadlock indefinitely; (b) the shared repo register - a stray docs/FOLLOWUPS.json.lock was found and removed, and deselecting all 19 tests that spawn a subprocess or write a repo file did NOT change the stall rate (1 of 3 still stalled), so that lock is a real contention point but not this cause; (c) my own new guards - the stalls predate them (the first two parallel runs stalled before any W507 guard existed); (d) order dependence - --dist load scatter was green on the runs that completed, so no order-dependent test beyond the one W498 fixed. STILL UNEXPLAINED: what all workers block on at once. WHERE TO LOOK NEXT: get a stack from a stalled worker (faulthandler in the controller does not reach xdist subprocesses - try PYTHONFAULTHANDLER with a per-worker dump, or py-spy against a live worker pid); check for Windows handle or process exhaustion, since six workers each build the full app (about 18s and 54MB each) and several tests spawn further subprocesses; and check whether the module-scoped client fixture's app construction can block when six copies start together. UNTIL THEN: the serial run is what a commit is trusted to, and -n 6 is for a fast read only. A tool that fails silently a third of the time is the instrument-that-cannot-fail defect inverted.
items.slot_source: it is the other half of FU-249, which W507 closed for the isolation and the measurement; this row carries the reliability that stops it being the default

items.title: Sample and count the persisted outputs written while cross-request recall was the default (FU-256's part (a))
items.why: FU-256's parts (b) and (c) were delivered in W507 under the Owner's ruling: a row written from an augmented prompt is now MARKED at all four gateway writers, and the recall block states its provenance limit where a reader meets it. Part (a) remains and is a MEASUREMENT, not a build: nobody has established what the W489 defect actually did while it was live. THE FACTS: W489 found query/stream/stream_meta inheriting augment=True, so 29 generation-class callers - including the nine-stage synthesis cascade, the CEO blueprint and the digital-twin modeller - had another request's content prepended and presented as analysis of their own subject. THE WORK: sample the persisted outputs of those 29 surfaces for text that plainly came from another request (the native floor's tell is a Domain: or Problem: label whose value belongs to a different subject) and COUNT how many are affected, so the disclosure the Owner chose can eventually name a population instead of the whole pool. WHY IT MATTERS: W507's disclosure is currently over-broad by necessity - a stored row carries no timestamp, so recall must warn about EVERY pre-W507 line rather than the affected ones. A count would let the warning narrow to what is true, and a warning that covers everything is one a reader learns to ignore.

items.title: The pre-flight's self-match check flags a test that reads ANOTHER file
items.why: scripts/selfcheck_diff.py reported 6 [selfmatch] leads against test_w509_the_method_gate_has_a_surface, all false: the assertions search the CONTENT OF ChangeControlAgency.tsx and TransformationDashboard.tsx, not the test's own text, and each was proven able to fail by a blind that deleted the tsx line. The check appears to trigger on any test that resolves a path from Path(__file__).parents[1], which is how every page-reading guard in the suite is written. A screen that reports noise as findings costs the attention the real ones need (M-VERIF-12): narrow it to assertions whose search SUBJECT is the test file itself.

items.title: The circadian intensity map never reaches metabolism, so the clock cannot modulate energy
items.why: heartbeat.py computes a circadian intensity of 1.0/0.7/0.5/0.3 by phase and uses it to gate auto_evolve. But biobus._update_atp passes ATPSimulator.update a circadian_efficiency of only 1.0 or 0.8 and nothing else, so the real map never reaches metabolism at all. atp_depletion_state() derives the consequence itself: min production 0.5*0.8 = 0.4 against max consumption 0.1*1.0 = 0.1, so can_deplete is False - a 4x gap. THE ORGANISM CANNOT DEPLETE BY ARITHMETIC, not by labelling. FIX (two parts): feed the real phase intensity into _update_atp, which drops min production to 0.15; and raise the consumption coefficient so sustained load can exceed it. CAUTION: this makes atp < _ATP_CONSERVE_AT (0.3) reachable for the FIRST time, which caps all cognition to max_parallel 1 - a live behaviour change on a path everything flows through. Ramp it.

items.title: The consultation contract forces an engine to fabricate, and cannot carry provenance
items.why: agentic_core/consultation/interface.py, measured: (a) ConsultationResponse.confidence is a REQUIRED float with ge=0/le=1 and no three-state option, so an engine that cannot judge its own confidence MUST invent a number - build six honest engines against this and you get six fabricated confidences, which is the defect P3.12 exists to remove, recreated by its own interface; (b) ValidationResult.passed is a bare bool, so a validation nothing performed must claim True or False, and all six engines currently pass passed=True; (c) there is NO provenance field at all - no served_by, no is_external - so once an engine calls a model the contract cannot say what served it, making the cognitive layer the one place twenty rounds of provenance work would stop; (d) the engine Literal lists SEVEN engines while registry.EngineType declares NINE. FIX THE CONTRACT BEFORE ANY ENGINE COMPUTES.

items.title: Customer/user satisfaction has no mechanism anywhere, and it gates selection
items.why: One of the four measures the vision states are continuously monitored, evaluated and improved. MEASURED across the whole codebase: exactly two occurrences of 'satisfaction' - a section HEADING in a generated management-systems document, and a hardcoded 'user_satisfaction: 1.0' in biomimicry/geospheric/drad.py whose monitor() updates it only from telemetry nothing ever passes. Nothing measures it and no plan item covers it. It is honest today only because nothing claims otherwise. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE GAP: selection between entities cannot honestly turn on until all four measures exist, because a composite built from the two that ARE measured (profitability, compliance) is selection on those two wearing a composite's clothes - and selection on the wrong measure creates optimisation pressure toward the proxy. So this row gates the whole of evolution. FIX: a real signal from real users, however small, and refuse to synthesise one.
items.slot_source: P3.27 SELECTION is the item that cannot begin until this exists: clause (2) IS this row, and clause (3) refuses while any of the four measures is unmeasured. It was slotted P2.4 as a truth-sweep row before the item existed.

items.title: The transformation cycle and the CCA record cannot hold a COMMITMENT, so a promise has no variance
items.why: Measured W514 by running the night's Round A through the real chain in an isolated store. What WORKS: POST /api/v1/cca/submit returns cca-48d92679ae at tier HIGH (per the FU-014 ruling that code_change is HIGH) with a real method_check citing lesson ids, scope_appraisal, health_gate and immune_threat_at_submit; the change appears in GET /api/v1/cca/queue - the queue the growing tip reads - carrying awaiting_board_ratification and board_ratification; POST /api/v1/transformation/orchestrate returns a method_check with MET/basis/checkable_from per requirement, an honestly scoped governance verdict ('intent + domain only ... the delivery content was NOT screened'), outcome_not_recorded, and the live products_services_catalogue. THE GAP: committed_rounds and confidence passed to /transformation/orchestrate were SILENTLY DROPPED (the response model strips undeclared keys), and neither the CCA record nor the queue nor GET /cca/{id} holds any commitment, confidence, variance, budget or capacity field. So Workstation can govern a change but cannot record what scope was promised, at what confidence, against what capacity, nor what the variance turned out to be - which is the one thing an entity working unattended between Owner reviews must carry. docs/CAPACITY_FACULTY_MODEL.md models the integration and notes the invariant it must not break: _prospect() refuses to attach probabilities to possibilities, and that refusal is correct for a branch about someone's DECISION while a measured self-throughput figure is a different class of claim.

items.because_means: the work this row asked for was done in this round, not found already done
items.close_note: A commitment is recorded AT SUBMIT (committed_rounds, confidence, a required basis) against a capacity the platform MEASURES from its own commit history (median 1.61h per round over 104 rounds at the time of building, with quartiles and sample size), and a VARIANCE is read back at the outcome. The design follows CAPACITY_FACULTY_MODEL section 2, which is permissive rather than prohibitive here: a probability about SELF is a measurement and one about another's choice is a fabrication, so a commitment about this platform's own delivery is admissible - but a number a CALLER supplies is not a measurement, so confidence is stored and RENDERED as DECLARED, and a commitment with no basis is REFUSED 422 rather than stored. The variance measures ELAPSED HOURS from the record's own stamps and derives a rounds figure only by dividing by a median it NAMES, because a round is not a clock unit; where no capacity was measured the rounds figure is None with a reason rather than a number. OrchestrateRequest declares the two fields that were being silently dropped and threads them to the change it files. The promise reaches the QUEUE (the list the growing tip reads, so it is visible while work is in flight) and the governance PAGE, with the declared/measured label on screen. Both of the two places that mark a change implemented call one helper, asserted over the AST so a third site added later is caught. AND THE PRE-FLIGHT CAUGHT ELEVEN KEYS OF MY OWN REACHING NO SURFACE: four were duplicates of fields that already render and were removed, four were the measured capacity and now reach the chip's title including the quartiles, one prose field was folded into the basis the title shows, and the stage echo's prose moved into the stage basis the page actually consumes. It also surfaced FOUR pre-existing sibling-return disagreements in the two functions this round touched - FU-334's class - and all four are fixed. 10 of 10 blinds red, re-run after the post-sweep edits.

items.title: A closure records no REASON, so retrospection cannot read why anything closed
items.why: W515 measured: scripts/followups.py close refuses any --by that is not a round id (W### or W###a), correctly, because a rate computed over prose would be invisible to every projection. But there is then NOWHERE in the register to record WHY a row closed - whether it was BUILT, or MEASURED as already satisfied, or PERFORMED with a not-assessable answer. Five rows closed in W515 are of three different kinds (FU-071/072/187/228 measured already-satisfied by earlier rounds; FU-302 performed with a NOT_ASSESSABLE population and a measured basis) and the register records all five identically. The consequence is specific: the Appraisal Cell's retrospection faculty (api/method.py _retrospect) reports the refutation share and which rounds only found work, and it CANNOT distinguish a round that built from a round that measured - so the item rate and the row rate both read a measurement close as if it were a build. THE WORK: an optional --because on close, stored as a field, with a small closed vocabulary (built | already_satisfied | performed_not_assessable | refuted) plus free text; _retrospect then reports the mix. A round that closes six rows by measuring them is not the same round as one that closes six by building, and the plan currently cannot tell.

items.title: D-SELECT cannot be adjudicated as its shape is written: 106 of 224 candidates are scalar clamps
items.why: W514 RAN the three defect-class screens over 496 files (agentic_core/**/*.py + the superapp src), which had never been done. Result: D-BEARER 0 candidates; D-THEATRE 15, ALL FIFTEEN ADJUDICATED AND DEFENDED (five are comments recording removed fabrication; seven are ordinary setTimeout clearing a copied/saved flag, a 35s request abort, or revokeObjectURL cleanup; one is Math.random as ID entropy; and NeuralLink.tsx drives a decorative synapse grid from Math.random on a 100ms timer but DISCLOSES it on the surface at line 77 - 'Synapse grid is a decorative animation - it is not measured activity' - checked at the render, not in the comment). So the tree is clean on both classes that carry signal. D-SELECT is the problem: 247 candidates, and the class declares its shape as 'a maximum or minimum taken over a collection' while its regex is \b(?:max|min)\s*\( which matches any call. Of 224 in agentic_core, 106 are numeric CLAMPS - max(0.0, 100.0 - cpu), min(1.0, x) - a maximum over two scalars, which is not a selection over a collection and fails the class's own definition before anyone reads it. Only 3 of 224 match the discriminating sub-shape, a sort followed by taking the first. THE WORK: narrow the shape to exclude a max/min whose first argument is a numeric literal, guarded by driving one clamp and one genuine selection so the exclusion cannot be vacuous, then adjudicate the ~118 survivors plus the 3 sorts. Adjudicating 247 by hand would be adjudicating a screen whose stated domain and whose regex disagree, which is why this row had never been completed: the work as written is unbounded.
items.slot_source: the screens and their harness ride P2.17; this is an instrument-precision fix, not a sweep row

Combined consequence: a reader sees THAT the ethical framework was assessed or not, never that one of its four dimensions was not - so FU-160's correction lands in the DCMS-sealed record and the API payload (consumed by board packs and exports) and changes nothing a page shows. items.title: The pre-flight's key screen reads a comparison as a dict key: any 'if x == "name":' fires it
items.why: W519 measured. scripts/selfcheck_diff.py:156 KEY_RE is '"([a-z_][a-z0-9_]{2,})"\s*:' - a quoted lowercase word followed by a colon. It cannot distinguish a dict key ('"satisfied": value') from an EQUALITY COMPARISON whose line ends in the statement colon ('if args.cmd == "satisfied":'). W519 added such a line and the screen reported the CLI subcommand name as 'a key produced but read by no surface', asking which page shows it. No page shows a subcommand name, and none should. The pattern fires on any 'if x == "some_word":' or 'elif'/'while'/'case' of the same shape, which is common in every dispatcher in this repository. THE WORK: require the colon not to be a statement terminator - either something non-empty must follow it on the same line, or the line must not begin with if/elif/while/case/match - and drive the fix with one dict key and one comparison so the exclusion cannot be vacuous. THIS IS THE THIRD PRECISION DEFECT IN THE SAME SCREEN FAMILY: FU-303 (selfmatch flagged a path-joined read of another file, reinstated W518 after a wrong revert) and FU-317 (D-SELECT counted 106 scalar clamps of 224 as selections over a collection). An instrument reporting noise as findings costs the attention the real ones need (M-VERIF-12), and a round that learns to ignore its pre-flight has lost the pre-flight.
items.slot_source: FU-262 already owns the pre-flight's coverage in cluster (d); this is its precision, in the same file

items.title: POST /api/v1/cognitive/cascade reports engines_run as the literal 6 - it counts nothing the cascade did
items.why: Found W520 while wiring /engines to the registry. cognitive.py's cascade response carries 'engines_run': 6 as a hard literal with a basis string reading 'the six implemented engines'. FU-223 was closed by adding that basis, but a basis beside a literal does not make the literal a measurement: the number is identical whether the cascade ran six engines, four, or none that produced anything. The cascade result itself is the only record of what happened and it is not consulted for this count. CONSEQUENCE: an engine that fails inside execute_cascade without raising still reads as having run, on a reached public route - the same shape as the nature-field-reporting-an-outcome class already recorded twice in this repo. THE WORK: derive engines_run from the cascade result's own per-engine entries, and where the result cannot say, report the count as not recorded rather than as six; a guard drives a cascade in which one engine yields nothing and asserts the reported count drops. NOTE the neighbouring literal already fixed this round: /engines' layer counts were the same shape and are now computed from the table, with the registry's own answer carried beside them.

items.title: A crash in the insights route renders as 'no projects yet' - the error key has no reader
items.why: Found W521 by the pre-flight's [returns] lead while completing FU-164's C10. products.py intelligence_insights() has three returns: the normal one carries insights, computed_at, total_projects and score_meaning; the empty-portfolio path appends an i-0 Onboarding insight; and the except branch returns insights:[] plus error and computed_at, omitting the other two. MEASURED READER: the only consumer of this route is apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/coe/KnowledgeHub.tsx (line 76), it reads data.insights only, and at line 171/198 an empty insights array renders 'Create projects to generate portfolio insights'. So an exception inside the computation - a store read failing, a project record missing a field - is shown to the user as the statement that they have no projects. A failure is being presented as a measured empty result, on a reached page, which is the class this repo has fixed repeatedly elsewhere. NOT a missing-key defect: nothing indexes total_projects or score_meaning off this route (the other total_projects hits in the frontend belong to the organism, capital and introspection routes), so the pre-flight's two leads are about a reader that does not exist; the error key having no reader is the real one. THE WORK: the except branch says the computation failed in a field the page reads, and the page distinguishes a failure from an empty portfolio rather than printing the onboarding line for both; a guard forces the exception (monkeypatch _all_projects to raise) and asserts the page's own distinguishing field is set, because a backend-only fix moves the lie one layer down.

items.title: The forecast dropped its batch line entirely when no batch existed, and a crash rendered as the same absence
items.why: Found W521 by the suite going RED on test_w501, which asserts both the BATCH and the BUNDLE line are present in render_forecast. Closing FU-164 closed the last open row citing a W477 sweep class, so batches() legitimately returned zero - and the renderer emitted the line only 'if _b:', so the line VANISHED. Three states were rendering as two: a batch exists, no batch exists, and the batch computation raised. The third borrowed the appearance of the second, because the 'except Exception: _b = []' above it produced the same empty list as success - a failure presented as a measured absence, which is the defect this generated page exists to prevent. Same shape in the bundle block. FIXED: both lines are always emitted; an absence states its reason; and a failure says the computation FAILED with the exception, so whether one exists is NOT KNOWN. A new guard (test_w521_a_failed_computation_is_not_reported_as_an_absence) monkeypatches each function to raise and asserts the line says NOT KNOWN, carries the exception type, and does NOT say the reassuring thing it says when the answer really is none - the distinction had no instrument behind it until this round, which is a claim without a test.

items.title: FU-242's premise is false: there is no PID regulator anywhere in geospheric/, and its file list names a module that no longer exists
items.why: Measured W521 while preparing P3.19, read-only. FU-242 says agentic_core/biomimicry/geospheric/ holds five real modules 'including a genuine PID regulator', and P3.19's body plans to bind six cycles 'through the geospheric regulators that already exist'. Both are wrong. (a) regulator.py (72 lines) is NOT a PID and its own docstring already says so, written by W516's FU-307 fix: integral_error is assigned once as a dict of zeros and never accumulated so there is no integral term, and dt is computed in regulate() and never read so there is no derivative term. It is a proportional comparator, and _compute_corrective_action RETURNS A STRING naming an action rather than applying one. (b) No sibling has one either: homeostatic_regulator.py (57) is threshold-scoring (load += 2.0 per breached biomarker), and balance_regulator.py (18) and drad.py (63) contain no integral or derivative term at all. Five modules, zero PID. (c) The file list is stale: resilience.py is named and DOES NOT EXIST (it was registered dead as FU-078), while orchestrator_legacy.py (31 lines) exists and is not named. CONSEQUENCE: three outside proposals assume a running PID control layer with plus/minus 5 percent tolerance over six cycles, and what exists is one proportional comparator that emits advice strings and is called by nothing. P3.19 is a BUILD, not a binding, and its own ACCEPT already protects the honest version - a setpoint is an aspiration until something measures the variable, and a gain is a default until tuned and the record says so. Correct the row and P3.19's body before the round starts, or its first hour disproves its own premise.

items.title: The six-stage recirculation loop CANNOT RUN: driving it from the heartbeat shows INTEND raising a TypeError
items.why: Found W532 by doing what P3.16's bar asks - wiring the loop to the heartbeat - which ran it for the first time. NOTHING HAD EVER RUN IT: execute_cycle has one caller (AvatarFrontendInterface) and nothing calls that caller, so every defect below was invisible to the whole suite. Three surfaced in sequence, each recorded by the beat rather than swallowed: (1) AvatarState requires avatar_id and user_id, which the orchestrator's own construction path never supplied; (2) the heartbeat resolves its logger through _ueg_logger() returning a UEGLogger, which has NO log_event method - the orchestrator and the clearance chain both call log_event, so the two logger interfaces differ and the loop cannot log through the heartbeat's; (3) THE BLOCKER: stage INTEND raises TypeError: object str can't be used in an await expression. TRACED TWO LEVELS: _stage_intend awaits self.uci.intercept(context, ratify); uci_interceptor.intercept awaits self.divine.calibrate_niyyah(...); and divine/v2/alignment_v2.py:32 declares calibrate_niyyah as async - so the await is correct on paper. THE OPEN QUESTION, which this round did not settle: what self.divine actually IS at runtime. The likely shape is an ImportError fallback substituting a stub whose method returns a string, which is exactly the TFEL fallback pattern recorded in FU-329 and found again in W530's Mock regulator - this repository has that defect in at least three places. NEXT STEP: print type(self.divine) and type(self.uci) inside a constructed orchestrator before changing anything, because a fallback that returns a str is a different fix from a signature mismatch. CONSEQUENCE FOR P3.16: its bar says the loop runs from the heartbeat. The drive is built and correctly reports the failure as a failure, but the loop is not runnable, so that clause is NOT met and the item stays open on it.

items.title: verify_output returns a bare SHA3-512 digest under the name merkle_proof
items.why: The avatar emission verifier returns hashlib.sha3_512(json.dumps(emission)).hexdigest() as the value of a key called merkle_proof. A digest of one object is not a Merkle proof: there is no tree, no sibling path and no root to verify an inclusion against, so nothing can be checked with it and no second party can use it to confirm the emission belongs to any log. This is the same class as the HMAC that was named a post-quantum signature in W514, and the same remedy applies: either compute an inclusion proof against a real append-only log, or name the field for the digest it actually is.

items.title: The round-start `satisfied` check cannot see a row that names no files
items.why: W534 repaired a crash in scripts/followups.py satisfied - it did `(_out.get('limits') or {}).items()` while every one of the ten producers in api/method.py emits `limits` as a PROSE SENTENCE, and `or {}` cannot defend against a wrong TYPE because a non-empty string is truthy. The command printed its results and THEN raised, so the failure looked cosmetic while the command exited non-zero at every round start. Repairing it surfaced the limit statement it had been suppressing, and that limit is the actual finding: the check reads only the last 400 commits and only commits whose subject declares a round, so A ROW CARRYING NO FILES IS INVISIBLE TO IT, as is a row found by a round the commit subject does not name. The round-start step that proposes which rows a later round may already have satisfied therefore has a population it never considers, and nobody was told. THE WORK: report the rows the check COULD NOT CONSIDER alongside the candidates, with their count, so an unexaminable row is visible as unexamined rather than absent - the same distinction this programme enforces everywhere else. FILES CORRECTED W536 and the work DONE: the row cited only scripts/followups.py, where W534 fixed the crash, while the blind spot itself lives in agentic_core/api/method.py's _rows_the_tree_moved_under. Both are now named. The check reports not_considered_rows, not_considered_row_count and commits_no_round_could_be_read_from beside its candidates, with a basis saying those rows are UNEXAMINED rather than cleared. MEASURED on the live register at close: 0 open rows name no files, and 39 of 400 commits read carry a subject the parser could not read a round from — so about a tenth of the history was invisible to the round-start step and nobody was told. The count is deliberately NOT split between a subject declaring no round and one declaring a sub-round the parser cannot read: those are different facts and this counts only what no round could be read from.

items.title: The VSB ledger keeps TWO sets of money figures that are maintained separately and can disagree, which is the economy's own no-second-store rule broken at its centre
items.why: Measured W543 while binding P3.19's water cycle to a figure the platform already measures, and the binding nearly reported a constant 0.0 because of it. VirtualLedger holds two money projections: _data['balances'] (the seven waterfall pots: revenue, reserves, owner, self_investment, capital_fund, user_projects, charity), returned by balances() and written by record() at ledger.py:445-452; and _data['accounts'] (the double-entry chart), written by _apply_posting at ledger.py:412-436 and summed by trial_balance(). DRIVEN ON A FRESH STORE: record('reserves', 750.0) leaves balances reserves=750.0 while trial_balance reports debit_side_total 0.0; a following post('revenue','reserves',500.0) leaves balances UNCHANGED at 750.0 while trial_balance reports -500.0 on both sides. So after two movements the same ledger answers 750 or -500 depending on which accessor is asked, and trial_balance still reports balanced:true because both of its sides moved together. CONSEQUENCE: any surface reading balances() misses every raw post(), and any surface reading trial_balance() misses every record(). The economy is live and reached (the §4 waterfall, the VSB cockpit, the §12 survival instinct), and P3.19's own ACCEPT forbids a second store of numbers. NOT FIXED HERE because changing what a money accessor means requires grepping every reader first (the field-meaning rule, W495). FIX: establish which projection is authoritative, make the other derive from it or state its scope in its own name, and add a leg that drives record() and post() in one ledger and asserts the two readings cannot diverge.
items.source: W543 (driven on a fresh store while binding the water cycle)
items.because_means: the work this row asked for was done in this round, not found already done
items.close_note: THE ROW'S PREMISE IS PARTLY REFUTED BY RE-DRIVING IT, and the real defect is sharper. The row read 'record(reserves,750) leaves the chart at 0.0' as the chart MISSING the entry. Re-driven on a fresh store: the chart records it in full - reserve_fund +750 and cash -750 - and the debit-side TOTAL is 0.00 because BOTH ARE ASSETS, which is the correct answer for moving cash into a reserve. trial_balance does not miss record(). THE REAL DEFECT, confirmed: post() took its account names through CHART.get(name,'asset'), so it silently invented any name it was handed. 'reserves' is a WATERFALL POT (a balances() key), not an account - so post('revenue','reserves',500) opened a phantom asset beside the real reserve_fund, which is exactly how the apparent divergence was produced. post() now REFUSES an off-chart name and the message names the pot confusion. MEASURED BEFORE REFUSING: every internal caller already passes chart accounts (the _COMPAT_POSTING pairs, retained_earnings on close, transfer_out/reserve_fund in transfers), so nothing in the tree breaks. Both accessors now state their scope, and the ONE consumer's basis - which had repeated the misreading - is corrected: the two are different projections of the same postings, so a difference between their totals is not a disagreement.

items.title: water_cycle is the outlier of the six: no base class, no sense(), and its own duplicate PIDController
items.why: Measured W543 while making the six cycles report honestly. Five of the six (carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, sulfur) extend GeosphericCycle and define sense(), so one implementation on the base class now answers for all five. HydrologicManager in agentic_core/biomimicry/cycles/water_cycle.py does not: (a) it extends nothing, so it inherits none of the three-state deviation, is_homeostatic or sense_reservoir work; (b) it defines NO sense(), so GET /api/v1/cycles reports a stated absence for it rather than a reading; (c) it declares its OWN PIDController class at water_cycle.py:4-15, a second copy of the controller in base_cycle.py with the same algorithm and no gains provenance — so the gains_tuned/gains_basis fields added this round do not exist on it; (d) its evaporate() and condense() mutate self.reservoirs with literal rates annotated 'Simulated max rate' and 'Simulated efficiency', and self.efficiency = 0.85 is a literal; (e) its regulate_homeostasis(current_temp) shows that its setpoint of 75.0 is a TEMPERATURE, which is why the route refuses to compute any deviation — the figure water is bound to is virtual WST. CONSEQUENCE: a second controller is a second place the control logic can drift, and the one cycle most likely to be read first (liquidity) is the one with no reading method. FIX: make HydrologicManager extend GeosphericCycle, delete its duplicate PIDController in favour of the shared one, give it a sense() through sense_reservoir, and either declare a unit for its setpoint or state that it has none.

items.title: Eight suite guards take the heartbeat module's reference where a reload splits it, and only a classification can say which of them are order-dependent flakes
items.why: Measured W549 after test_w545 failed its THIRD full run on a latent order-dependent flake. THE MECHANISM: test_w420_autonomy_settings_survive_a_restart calls importlib.reload on agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py, which re-runs 'heartbeat = OrganismHeartbeat()' and rebinds the module attribute to a NEW object, while agentic_core/api/heartbeat.py still holds the reference it bound when the app was built. From then on the module's heartbeat and the route's are two different objects, so a guard that MUTATES the module's one and ASSERTS THROUGH A ROUTE configures one object and reads another. W503 documented this against test_w503b and the remedy is one line (import agentic_core.api.heartbeat and take its .heartbeat), but it was fixed only where it had been caught. MEASURED NOW: 8 guards in integration_tests/test_mvp_spine.py import 'from agentic_core.organism.heartbeat import heartbeat' (lines 1504, 5274, 5728, 5832, 9565, 17027, 23586, 25376) and only 2 take the route's reference. THE TRAP BITES ONLY A GUARD THAT DOES BOTH — mutates the object and asserts through a route — so these must be CLASSIFIED, not mass-edited: a guard that only reads the object, or only asserts on the object directly, is correct as written and changing it would be churn. WHY IT HID SO LONG: test_w545 passed alone and in FOUR consecutive full runs, because xdist distributes dynamically and happened to put the two tests on different workers; and reproducing it needs a client-using test ordered BEFORE the reload, so the app is built against the pre-reload object. A first reproduction attempt with just the two tests passed and nearly cleared the diagnosis. FIX: classify all 8, convert only those that mutate-and-assert-through-a-route, and add a leg that fails when a guard does both while holding the module's reference. The discriminating selector costs 18 seconds ('owner_scoped or w420 or w545') against an 11-minute suite, so each candidate can be proven individually.

items.title: Horizon's kernel is built and reached by its own routes, but the SEAM the item names is not wired: no middleware fronts the domain routes and no hook sits at record_outcome
items.why: Measured W550, which built P2.11's kernel. ALL THREE ACCEPT CLAUSES ARE MET: each compression state and each decision state is reachable and asserted (NOT_COMPRESSED and ESCALATE through the route on the ordinary path, COMPRESSED and PROCEED through the route with a model-served provenance supplied, NOT ASSESSABLE from a record that cannot be read), the floor's run produces NOT_COMPRESSED with a reason that states it is the common path, and no field is filled by inference (the five compression fields are ABSENT rather than empty on an uncompressed record, and a model that answers partially does not have the rest defaulted). WHAT IS NOT BUILT is the item body's own seam sentence: a middleware in front of the domain routes plus a hook where the run paths already call operational_excellence.record_outcome. Today Horizon observes only what is POSTed to /api/v1/horizon/observe, so it is a membrane nothing passes through - the same reach gap W543 found in the six biogeochemical cycles, where the code existed and no live path reached it. record_outcome is at agentic_core/api/operational_excellence.py:50 and is called best-effort by the run paths, so the hook has a real attachment point. THE MIDDLEWARE NEEDS A DECISION, which is why it is filed rather than built: a membrane in FRONT of the domain routes that returns ESCALATE on the ordinary path would refuse every request this platform serves, because nothing compresses and the fail-closed rule escalates an unknown domain. So the middleware must either observe-and-record WITHOUT gating (honest, and the decision becomes a fact on the record rather than a block), or gate only a named list of grave routes. The first is the smaller claim and is almost certainly right, but it means the word membrane describes something that observes rather than something that stops - and that is the Owner's distinction to confirm, not mine.

items.title: The distress route list is the one field P2.12 closes WITHOUT, and nothing yet records that it must arrive with its reviewer
items.why: W551 built P2.12's three gates and its bar is met: every refusal path is driven, each gate's limit is on the surface, and the distress routes render as NOT SUPPLIED visibly on a page as well as a route. THE BAR CLOSES ON THAT BY THE OWNER'S OWN RULING (FU-270): 'P2.12 closes on its refusal paths with the unfilled field visible on the surface, and the list is supplied later with its reviewer.' So the item is DONE and the platform still cannot name a human route to anyone in distress. THAT IS THE DELIVERY THIS ROW HOLDS OPEN, because an item marked done is where a deferred obligation goes to be forgotten. WHAT IS IN PLACE: DISTRESS_ROUTES is an empty tuple in agentic_core/gaas/v5/horizon_guardrails.py; every gate response carries human_routes None with a basis saying the field is unfilled and why; the page at /horizon-guardrails renders NOT SUPPLIED in large type with the backend's own sentence beneath it; and a guard leg asserts that NO digit sequence resembling a telephone number exists in the gate module, the route module or the page, because a fabricated helpline is the one fabrication no later correction reaches the person who dialled it. WHAT ARRIVING LOOKS LIKE: the Owner supplies the routes WITH THEIR REVIEWER - a named person or body who checked that each route is real, current and appropriate to the jurisdiction - and each entry is stored with that reviewer and the date they checked it, so a route can later be shown to be stale rather than silently trusted. The guard's no-number leg must then be narrowed to the two modules that still hold none, NOT deleted, and a new leg must assert every supplied route carries its reviewer. UNTIL THEN THE HONEST STATE IS THE CURRENT ONE: this platform withholds AI counsel, says plainly it is not a person, and cannot tell anyone where to turn.
