items.title: The parallel-suite stall RECURRED and was measured live: six idle workers at 91 percent, and the progress instrument undercounted by a factor of six
items.why: FU-301 has recorded an unexplained stall since W507 and asked for a stack from a live stalled worker. W552's suite stalled and was caught ALIVE, so these are the first measurements taken from one rather than inferred afterwards. (a) TIMING: started 08:40:20, still alive at 09:33:43 - 53 minutes against a mean of 10.6 minutes measured over the fourteen completed runs of this night (range 9m36s to 11m16s). (b) POSITION: the terminal had emitted 544 progress characters of an expected 549, i.e. it stalled at about 91 percent with no F and no E - matching W507's observed 74/89/57 percent stalls. (c) STATE: seven processes alive (one controller, six workers). CPU time sampled twice eight seconds apart was FROZEN for six of the seven; the seventh moved 0.08s, which is a controller poll and not work. So every worker is idle simultaneously - W507's description confirmed exactly, and still not a single slow test. (d) RATE: ONE STALL IN FIFTEEN RUNS tonight, where W507 measured three in six. So it is far rarer than when the row was written and it is NOT fixed, which means the -n 6 cadence remains sound only because the completeness gate catches it. (e) A NEW FINDING ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT, not the stall: the progress file read {collected: null, reported: 93} while 544 tests had produced a terminal character. So in a stalled run the hook reports no collected total and undercounts the reported set roughly six-fold. run_verdict therefore answered NOT KNOWN, which is the correct verdict - but it reached it because no collected count existed, NOT because a short reported count was compared against a known total, which is how it was designed to detect this. A gate that returns the right answer by the wrong route will return the wrong answer when the route changes. (f) NO STACK WAS OBTAINED: py-spy is not installed and is not on PATH, so the row's stated next step is still open - and the next live stall should be used for it before killing, since this is evidently a once-in-fifteen opportunity. FIX: install py-spy so the next stall yields a stack; and separately, make the progress hook's collected count survive a stalled xdist run, since that is the figure the completeness gate is supposed to compare against.  THIRD LIVE RECURRENCE, MEASURED W558 AND THE SHARPEST EVIDENCE SO FAR. The run stalled at 543 of 555 tests - twelve left - and sat there with its output file unwritten for 14.4 minutes. The decisive measurement, which earlier recurrences did not have: CPU time across ALL SEVEN processes (one controller, six workers) moved 0.03 SECONDS IN 10 WALL-SECONDS. They are not spinning, not contending for a lock and not slowly finishing - they are doing nothing at all. Their working sets had also been trimmed to 4.8-27 MB, which a process holding a built FastAPI app with 507 routes cannot be while it is working, so they had been idle long enough for Windows to page them out. AND TWO TESTS HAD ALREADY FAILED before the stall (F at 90 percent), whose names are UNKNOWN because pytest never reached its summary - so a stall also costs the diagnosis of whatever else went wrong in the same run. Killed by PID; every changed .py re-parsed intact afterwards. THE PATTERN ACROSS THREE SIGHTINGS: W507 about one run in three; W552 at 91 percent with six workers CPU-frozen; W558 at 98 percent with twelve tests left. Always LATE in the run, always with workers idle rather than busy, and never at the same test - which argues against one slow test and for the controller and the workers losing each other near the end of the queue.

items.title: The validator interface is synchronous and one of the four real checks is async, so hallucination_containment can never assess on the live path
items.why: Measured W553 while giving the declared constitutional constraints their instruments. UniversalEnforcementPattern calls validator.validate(target, context) SYNCHRONOUSLY, and HallucinationSandbox.validate_output is async because it awaits a UEG log (agentic_core/governance/gaas/v5/hallucination_sandbox.py). So the validator calls asyncio.run, which raises RuntimeError whenever an event loop is already running - and the live path is always inside one, because VRPR's process() is async and is called from the recirculation loop. DRIVEN: calling the chain from inside the orchestrator reports hallucination_containment as unassessable with 'an event loop is already running, so the sandbox was not called', while calling the same validator from synchronous test code assesses it normally. So one of the four constraints that HAS an instrument can only ever assess outside the path that matters. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: replicating the sandbox's two heuristics inside the validator. That would create a SECOND screen over the same subject, which is the defect the delegation was chosen to avoid - and the two copies would drift. THE HONEST STATE IS REPORTED, which is why this is a row and not a bug: the validator says exactly why it did not run, and the chain distinguishes 'no instrument' from 'an instrument that was not given its input', so a reader sees that this one is the second kind. FIX: add an async path to the enforcement pattern (validate_async awaiting any validator that declares itself async, with the sync path unchanged for the rest) and call it from the async callers; or make the sandbox's heuristics a sync function that the async wrapper logs around, so one implementation serves both. The second is smaller and keeps a single screen.
items.source: W553 (driven on both the sync and the async path)

items.title: The clearance chain constructs an enforcement pattern and never calls validate on it, so its registration is not load-bearing
items.why: Measured W553 by grepping the chain's own body: agentic_core/avatars/core/clearance_chain.py mentions `enforcement` three times - the import, the construction with fail_on_missing_validator False, and the register_all call - and NEVER `self.enforcement.validate(...)`. So the nineteen validators registered there are registered onto an object the chain does not consult. DRIVEN, and this is what makes the row precise rather than a reading: constructing the real chain and the real orchestrator shows both patterns holding 19 validators, and driving the orchestrator's VRPR pipeline returns a verification_basis naming the figures ('2 of 19 declared constraint(s) were assessed', 15 with no instrument, 2 lacking their input) - so the ORCHESTRATOR's pattern is live and reaches a surface, and the chain's is not consulted at all. WHY THIS IS A ROW AND NOT A DELETION: gate 5 (Tahqeeq) verifies supplied constraints and an enforcement pattern in the chain is plausibly what it was constructed for, so removing it would delete an intention rather than a defect. WHY IT IS NOT HARMLESS EITHER: `chain.enforcement_registry` is a populated dict that reads exactly like enforcement, so a later reader - or a later basis string - could cite it as evidence the chain enforces the constitution when nothing in the chain has consulted a single validator. THE CONSTRUCTION SITE NOW SAYS SO in a comment, which is the interim honesty, not the fix. FIX: decide whether the chain should consult it (and if so, as which gate, with its refusal driven and its verdict carried into ClearanceResult.reason like every other gate's), or whether the pattern belongs only to the orchestrator and the chain should hold none.

items.title: A guard that pins a slot id or a component's rank fails the moment the plan moves, and it fails in the direction that punishes progress
items.why: Measured W554: closing P2.11 and two of its rows turned TWO suite guards red WITHOUT TOUCHING THE CODE EITHER OF THEM GUARDS. (1) test_w510 asserted `set(blocked_by_ruling) >= {P2.11, P2.16}` - a static set mirroring plan state. P2.11 became DONE, and a DONE item is correctly no longer blocked (the W551 correction to the cell itself), so the guard failed for the one reason it should have celebrated. (2) test_w500b asserted that the LARGEST file-connected component crosses items. Closing rows left two components tied at size 4 and the one the sort put first sat inside P2.17, so a true statement about the bundler failed on a TIE-BREAK. Both are now computed: w510 derives the expected blocked set from _BLOCKED_BY_RULING minus the plan's done markers and asserts the RELATION (no done item blocked, no item both blocked and closable), and w500b recomputes items_advanced independently for every component and asserts the crossing property over the SET rather than over whichever component ranks first. Both rewrites are blinded (20 of 20 BLIND(red) in W554). THE CLASS, which is what this row is for: a guard may not pin an identifier or an ordinal that the plan's own progress changes. It is worse than an ordinary stale assertion because it fails ON SUCCESS - every round that closes an item pays for it, and the cost is paid at the END of the round, after the full suite, which is the most expensive moment to discover anything. FIX: a pre-flight screen in scripts/selfcheck_diff.py that flags a CHANGED test asserting a literal plan-slot id (P<digit>.<digit>) or indexing a sorted collection at [0] and asserting a property of that element, and a sweep of the EXISTING guards for the same two shapes - this round found two by being bitten, and nobody has looked for the rest. THE SWEEP THIS ROW ASKED FOR HAS NOW BEEN RUN (W555), and a THIRD instance had already fired before it was: test_w535 asserted route_row sends an agentic_core/mjm/ row to "P3.16", and W555 closed P3.16 and handed its routes to P3.20. MEASURED over integration_tests/test_mvp_spine.py: 30 assertion lines carry a quoted plan-slot id, and MOST ARE SAFE, which is the useful half of the result — plan ORDER assertions (slots.index("P1.1") < slots.index("P1.14")) do not move with progress; synthetic registers (P9.9, P0.1, and the constructed two-component fixture) are fixtures and not state; "{P1.1, P1.11, P1.12} <= done" is monotone, since an item never un-closes; a CLOSED row's slot is frozen (FU-045, FU-063 on the done P2.9); and a declared property such as P4.1's delivered_by == owner-switch is not progress-dependent. SIX ARE AT RISK and each fails the moment its slot closes or its route is handed on: test_mvp_spine.py:15641, :15644 and :15656 assert route_row(...)["slot"] == "P2.4"; :15648 asserts an avatars route lands on "P3.6"; :18622 asserts P2.4's rounds_projected is None, which flips the first time P2.4 closes enough rows to be measurable; and :18713 asserts every batch slot equals "P1.18", an item that is already DONE. P2.4 and P3.6 are both open today, so none of the six is failing yet — which is exactly why they are worth fixing before a round pays for them at the end of a suite. THE FIX FOR EACH is the one W554 and W555 used three times: derive the expected slot from the ROUTES or the plan's own done markers and assert the RELATION (routes by area, severity does not change the destination, the claiming route points at an OPEN item) rather than the identity. FIFTH AND SIXTH INSTANCES, W560, AND THE FIFTH IS A NEW SHAPE: the stale thing was a FIXTURE, not an assertion. test_w512 submitted a change with affected_systems ["agentic_core/cognitive"] and required a scope to be appraised from it; exactly one open row cited that path - FU-275 - and closing FU-275 is what W560 set out to do. So the guard went red because the work succeeded, and no assertion in it named a slot id at all. THE SWEEP THIS ROW ALREADY CARRIES WOULD NOT HAVE FOUND IT: it scanned assertion lines for a quoted plan-slot id, and a fixture naming a FILE PATH that happens to be cited by one open row matches no such pattern. So the screen this row asks for must cover a second shape - a test input whose meaning depends on the register's current contents - and the honest way to find those is not a regex but the question "what in this test stops being true when a row closes?". FIXED by taking the path from a row that is open NOW, and by driving BOTH arms: an area an open row names must be appraised, and an area none names must report no scope with the reason. The second arm is exactly the state agentic_core/cognitive is in after W560, and it is now blinded. THE SIXTH instance was in the same round and is the ordinary shape: two legs of test_w510 and test_w512 had no arm for the Owner sequencing gate being DISCHARGED, fixed in W558. RUNNING TOTAL: six guards have gone red on the plan advancing rather than on a defect, across four rounds - W554 (2), W555 (1), W558 (2), W560 (1) - each costing a full suite re-run at the most expensive moment in the round.

items.title: The avatar path is held until the engines have a model path, and after W554 no open row held that obligation at all
items.why: Found W555 by checking my own previous round. W554 closed FU-357 by amending P3.16's third ACCEPT clause: the avatar path is HELD until the engines have a model path (P3.20), on the Owner's decision, rather than wired now - because the loop WITHHOLDS every emission today, so wiring it would turn a chat surface that answers into one that deliberately delivers nothing. The amendment is right and it is recorded. WHAT WAS WRONG IS THAT NOTHING CARRIED THE DEFERRED WORK FORWARD: FU-357 was closed, no open row mentioned the avatar path or avatar_interface.py, and the obligation existed only as prose inside the bar of an item that is itself about to be marked DONE. That is the precise failure FU-361 was filed against in W551 - 'an item marked done is where a deferred obligation goes to be forgotten' - committed one round later in my own work. THE MEASURED STATE, unchanged by the hold: agentic_core/avatars/frontend/avatar_interface.py is the only caller of execute_cycle for a USER rather than for the organism; agentic_core/avatars/__init__.py exports the orchestrator and not the interface; no route reaches either. So a module that would wire the avatar path exists and is reached by nothing. WHAT RELEASES THIS ROW: P3.20 giving the engines a path to a model, after which clearance gate 1 can receive a constitutional verdict and the loop can emit rather than withhold. WHAT THE WORK IS THEN: export the interface, give it a route, and drive BOTH outcomes - an emission that clears and one that is withheld - because a chat surface wired to a loop that can still withhold must show the withholding as a refusal with its reason and never as an empty answer. UNTIL THEN THE HOLD STANDS and this row is what makes it visible rather than remembered. RELEASE CONDITION MET ON ITS WORDS AND NOT IN SUBSTANCE — MEASURED W560, AND THIS NOW NEEDS THE OWNER. This row says it is released by "P3.20 giving the engines a path to a model, after which clearance gate 1 can receive a constitutional verdict and the loop can emit rather than withhold". W560 GAVE THEM THE PATH: all six engines now call the tier router and carry what served them. BUT THE CONSEQUENCE DID NOT FOLLOW. On this machine the router walks down to the deterministic floor, because no tier above it holds a resource - nothing is pulled and reachable, and the higher tiers are not runnable here for measured reasons (FU-271 default (a), the Owner decision of 2026-10-03). DRIVEN: every engine returns constitutional_validation.passed=None with the basis "no constitutional check ran: this engine performs none", so clearance gate 1 receives NO verdict and still withholds every emission - exactly as before. Wiring the avatar path today would therefore still turn a chat surface that answers into one that deliberately delivers nothing, which is the user-facing regression the Owner already declined once (FU-357, W554). THE QUESTION, which only the Owner can settle because only the Owner set the condition: the hold said "until the engines have a model path" and they now have one that ends at the floor. (a) HOLD, and correct this row's release condition to the substance rather than the wording - the avatar path waits until an engine can actually produce a constitutional verdict, which needs a model that answers, which needs FU-271 option (b) hardware or (c) an Owner-gated external accelerant. (b) WIRE IT NOW and let the honest refusal show on the chat surface, accepting that it delivers nothing until a model answers. DEFAULT IF UNDECIDED: (a) HOLD, for the same reason the Owner accepted in W554 - more honest and a user-facing regression is still a regression. Marked owner_gated so it is recorded rather than scheduled, and so it does not block P3.20, whose own three ACCEPT clauses are met.

items.title: The recirculation loop cannot be switched on from a running backend: auto_metabolic defaults off, the configure route does not expose it, and no page shows it
items.why: Found W555 by the FRESH-BACKEND PROBE P3.16's bar asks for, which is what a probe is for - the suite drives this loop by setting the attribute in process and could never have found it. MEASURED on a live uvicorn at :8010: POST /api/v1/heartbeat/configure accepts interval_seconds, auto_evolve, auto_economy, auto_align, auto_compliance and auto_ship, and NOT auto_metabolic; agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py:174 sets self.auto_metabolic = False at construction; heartbeat.py:369 gates the whole six-stage recirculation leg on it; and a POST /beat with the body {auto_metabolic: true, metabolic_every: 1} returns 200 while the field is silently ignored - the actions list comes back as pulse, homeostasis, genome_scan, transformation_tick and the metabolic cycle never runs. GET /status DOES report last_metabolic and metabolic_basis, so a reader sees a loop that never ran and no way to make it run. WHY THIS IS NOT A BUG IN W533: the loop genuinely runs from the beat and its stage latencies are genuinely recorded - that is driven, and the default being OFF is deliberate and right (six stages with their engine calls is expensive, and a surprise default that costs a second per beat would be the worse mistake). WHAT IS MISSING IS THE SWITCH: a capability nobody can turn on from outside the process is the reach class this plan keeps finding, one step short of a module nothing imports. ALREADY SCOPED, which is why this row is small: docs/CLOSURE_PREP_TWELVE.md item D7 sets out the work - add auto_metabolic to ConfigureRequest and to the heartbeat's _AUTONOMY_KEYS so it survives a restart, report it from status(), and add a sixth AUTONOMY entry plus the withheld state to HeartbeatMonitor.tsx. It also records a hazard found while scoping: adding the key to _AUTONOMY_KEYS breaks two existing guards through the shared store, so that half needs its own measurement. AND ONE BAR FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: a leg must assert the switch GATES the run - that with auto_metabolic false the cycle does NOT happen - because a leg that only drives the enabled case cannot tell a switch from a decoration.

items.title: P2.17's body states the round-cost measurement that IS the item, and every figure in it is now stale by a factor of two to four
items.why: Measured W555 while reporting the plan's state. P2.17's body carries its measurement as prose: 'median round 4.1 h over 32 commit-to-commit gaps; the full suite 46 min of it (~19%); the blind sweep ~10 min (~4%); the remaining ~77% is measuring live state, patching, writing guards and refuting' and '18 items carry a DONE marker across 18 DISTINCT rounds... 30 of the 48 rounds closed none at all'. LIVE TODAY, from the register's own generated block and from this session's runs: the median round is 1.6 h over 36 gaps (not 4.1 over 32); a full suite run is 10-17 min (14 runs this session, mean ~10.6 min when the tree is quiet), not 46; 38 items carry a DONE marker, not 18; and the suite's share of a round is therefore nearer 10-18% of a much shorter round. The direction of the error matters: the body argues that the lever is NOT working faster inside a round because verification is only ~19% of it, and both terms of that argument have moved - the round got shorter and the suite got much shorter, so the proportion the argument rests on was recomputed by the very work the item describes. WHY THIS IS INSIDE THE BAR RATHER THAN BESIDE IT: part (c) already reads 'the round-cost figures are computed from git and the register, never typed', and these are typed. So this row is not new scope - it is the measured instance that shows (c) is unmet in the item's own body, recorded so the closing round does not have to re-derive it. WHAT THE CLOSING ROUND SHOULD DO: render these figures from scripts/session_forecast.py or the register's generated block at render time, exactly as the pace block already does, so the paragraph cannot go stale again - and keep the ARGUMENT separate from the figures, because the argument (rounds that close no item, and a round that cannot close two) survives the recomputation while the percentages do not. MEASURED W558, AND THE SUITE PROFILE EXISTS FOR THE FIRST TIME: a full run was taken with --durations=30 folded into a re-run that was needed anyway, so it cost nothing. 30 of 554 tests hold 2,024 of the 4,529 worker-seconds available (754.77s wall x 6 workers) - FORTY-FIVE PER CENT OF ALL COMPUTE IN FIVE PER CENT OF THE TESTS. The slowest single test is test_w502 at 157.74s, which is a HARD FLOOR: no amount of parallelism finishes the suite faster than its longest test, so -n beyond 6 cannot help. The top five are test_w502 157.74s, test_w452 148.16s, test_cross_tenant_isolation_under_auth 115.19s, test_w462 112.13s and test_w479 110.48s = 644 worker-seconds between them. Four of the five drive real multi-stage lifecycles end to end, so they are expensive because they do the work rather than because they waste it - which means the honest lever is PLACEMENT (shard the heavy five across workers deliberately instead of letting xdist place them) and not optimisation. items.title: A stage with no prompt template yields its START event and then nothing, so a reader sees a stage begin and never finish
items.why: Found W558 while ANSWERING FU-338's open question rather than fixing it, which is what that row asked for. FU-338 asked whether _provenance_summary's calls=0 can mean 'a writer failed to append' instead of 'no call was made'. MEASURED and the answer is NO, so it closed as refuted: agentic_core/api/intelligence.py:513 is the only path that skips provs.append (a stage whose prompt template is empty hits `continue`), and all four engines declare every template they need - _APIE_STAGES 9 of 9, _BDP_STAGES 8 of 8, _DDPIE_STAGES 9 of 9, _SPI_STAGES 8 of 8 - so the writer is always reached today. And even on that path the zero would be TRUE, because a skipped stage makes no call, so not counting it is correct. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND INSTEAD: the `continue` at :513 comes AFTER `yield _ev(f'{stage_key}_start', stage_label, stage_desc)` at :509. So a stage whose template is missing announces that it has STARTED and then emits nothing - no result event, no failure, no reason - and the completion line reports it only as part of 'N of M stages ran', with no word about which one did not or why. A reader watching the stream sees a stage begin and silently never finish, which is the one thing a progress stream must not do: an absent ending is indistinguishable from a stream that was cut off. NOT LIVE TODAY, because no template is missing - this is a latent gap, recorded because the guard against it is cheap and the failure is silent. FIX: either emit a stage event carrying the skip and its reason before continuing, so the stream closes every stage it opens, or move the template check ABOVE the start event so a stage that cannot run is never announced. The second is smaller; the first tells a reader more.

items.title: OWNER DECISION: may the platform hold a behavioural model of an individual, to build the user-satisfaction signal the vision requires
items.why: W563 assessed the archived biomimetic layer and found the only user-satisfaction mechanism that exists anywhere in this repository or its archive. Its explicit half is a rating channel and is buildable now. ITS OTHER HALF IS THE QUESTION: it collects IMPLICIT feedback - a person's dwell time - and fits a per-user preference model to that person's own behaviour. It passes Ruling A.9.5 as it stands, because it forms no verdict on anyone's spiritual state and no verdict on a person at all; it is a preference, not a judgement. THAT IS PRECISELY WHY IT MUST BE ASKED BEFORE A REBUILD RATHER THAN AFTER: the one-question test is whether the SUBJECT IS A PERSON, and here it is - the model is of an individual, fitted from their behaviour, held by the platform. A ruling permitting it would be the first time this platform models a person at all, and that is a constitutional step, not an engineering choice. THE DECISION: (a) the explicit rating only - a person says what they think and nothing is inferred from how they behaved (the default, and what is built today); (b) explicit plus implicit signals used only in AGGREGATE, never attributed to an individual and never stored per person, so the platform learns about the product and not about anyone; (c) a per-individual model, which needs its own terms - what is collected, what it is used for, whether the person can see it, correct it and delete it, and whether it is ever used to decide anything about them. The vision names customer/user satisfaction as one of four continuous measures and the selection item refuses while any of the four is unmeasured, so (a) does unblock the measure. Nothing beyond (a) is written while this is open, and a guard leg greps the live tree for the behavioural signal rather than trusting the sentence.

items.title: Every other word-and-phrase screen on the platform is unaudited by the method that just found a live miss in the distress gate
items.why: W564 drove ten direct phrasings through the clinical-care gate and found that the plainest one - 'end my life' - PASSED the screen, while 'kill myself' escalated correctly. The pattern was `(?:end|take)\s+(?:my\s+own\s+)?life` : 'my' and 'own' were one optional unit, so it matched 'end life' and 'end my own life' and not the phrasing in between. It is fixed and guarded. THE LESSON IS THE METHOD, AND IT HAS NOT BEEN APPLIED ANYWHERE ELSE: a word screen is not reviewable by eye - the defect was invisible in the regex and obvious the moment the gate was driven with the phrasings it exists to catch. UNAUDITED BY THAT METHOD: _RULING_PATTERNS and _PROOF_PATTERNS in the same module, and - much larger - the three-regex keyword filter that the whole-vision document records as the ONLY screen on 49 of 57 API modules ('GaaS gate on every output: true for 8 of 57'). THE FIX: for each screen, enumerate the phrasings it is FOR, drive them, and record which pass - then either widen the pattern or move the phrasing into the declared coverage limit, because a screen that misses a phrasing it was written for is a defect while a screen that misses one it never claimed is a stated limit. Do not merely add patterns: the deliverable is the DRIVEN LIST, so the next round can tell the two apart.

items.title: Nine write paths use a TOLERANT read as their write base, so the write persists the recoverable prefix and destroys the rest
items.why: DRIVEN AND PROVEN in W577 on a user's own document. read_json_reported recovers a store's first complete JSON value via raw_decode and DISCARDS everything after it; nine functions take that value and hand it straight to atomic_write_json, so the discarded remainder is overwritten and gone. Driven: a user_workspace store holding two concatenated records (267 bytes, the shape a non-atomic overwrite of a shorter document by a longer one leaves) went through PUT /profile and came back 226 bytes with history=[] and prefs={} - the user's recorded question permanently destroyed - and the response reported success with no indication of any loss. THE NINE: api/agent_hub.py update_handoff_status (inside store_lock, so it is the authoritative write), api/operational_excellence.py set_health_baseline (would drop every OTHER model's baseline), api/user_workspace.py put_workspace + put_profile + clear_profile, api/native_ai.py evaluate_model + promote_model + retire_model + reinstate_model (all four via lifecycle_state -> save_lifecycle, dropping retired models and evaluations). THIS IS NOT FU-298's CLASS and must not be closed by it: FU-298 is a reader that does not disclose a short figure, which is a truth defect; this is a WRITER that destroys data it could not read, which is a loss defect, and surfacing a reason does not fix it. The remedy is the opposite one - a write base must be read STRICTLY and the write REFUSED, which is the rule capital_fund.py already states in writing for exactly this reason ('a WRITER asks strictly and refuses, because writing back over a quarantined store is how the reset becomes permanent') and which the other five files do not follow. LATENT VS LIVE: every in-platform writer is atomic (W472), so the platform cannot currently produce the concatenated shape itself; it is reachable through any corruption of external origin (a truncated restore, a partial sync, a copy interrupted mid-write), and the correct engineering answer does not depend on which - a tolerantly-read value is never a safe write base.

items.title: Every request model on the platform silently discards a field a caller sends, so an instruction and a dropped instruction look identical
items.why: MEASURED in W577 while preparing FU-313: 206 request/response models derive BaseModel across 60 files in agentic_core/api, and ZERO declare extra=forbid. Pydantic v2 ignores undeclared fields by default, so a caller can send a field, receive 200, and have it discarded with no indication - which is exactly FU-313's mechanism (committed_rounds and confidence sent to /transformation/orchestrate vanish because OrchestrateRequest declares neither) generalised to every route. The caller cannot distinguish a recorded instruction from a dropped one, and on a governance or commitment route that difference is the whole content of the request. THE REMEDY IS NOT A BLANKET FORBID and this row must not be read as asking for one: flipping 206 models would answer 422 to any caller sending an extra field, the frontend included, for no gain in truth on most of them. The work is to forbid on the models where an undeclared field means a LOST INSTRUCTION - commitments, budgets, governance inputs, anything a caller sends expecting it to be recorded - to leave the rest tolerant, and to SAY WHICH AND WHY, so the choice is auditable rather than a default nobody chose. FU-313 is the first instance and should declare its two fields regardless; this row is the class behind it.

items.title: An item holding routes can only be closed by handing ALL of them to one destination, which is how a sink is made
items.why: MEASURED IN W581, when P2.18's three clauses were all delivered and the item still could not be marked done. followups.py done P2.18 --reroute REFUSES with: "7 route(s) still send new rows to P2.18: pass --hand-to <the open item that owns that area now>". And --hand-to takes exactly ONE item. So the mechanism's only way to close an item that holds routes is to move ALL of them to a single destination, which is the definition of a sink. THIS IS HOW P2.4 BECAME ONE. Its own charter records it: nine of eleven open rows arrived AFTER its bar was written, through routes handed in when P1.16, P2.6, P2.8, P2.9, P3.18 and P3.19 closed, and the Owner ruled on 2026-10-02 that HIGH rows must route BY AREA precisely because that short-circuit is why P2.4 never closed. P2.18 then inherited all seven of those routes by the same single-target mechanism, and is now in the same position one item later. THE SEVEN AREAS HAVE NO OPEN OWNER BETWEEN THEM: autonomous technical support, the geospheric regulators and the causal simulator, the perimeter and the governance gate, the cascade's delivery measurement, the economy's flows, the catalogue and product directories (the largest, spanning forty files), and the developer pages' export surfaces. Every original owner is CLOSED, which is exactly why the rows keep landing wherever the mechanism last pointed. SO THE DECISION IS NOT A ROUND'S TO MAKE: handing seven unrelated areas to one open item recreates the condition the Owner has already ruled against, and splitting them by area is a thing the CLI cannot currently express. THE WORK, and it is two separable pieces. (1) THE MECHANISM: let an item's routes be handed per-route rather than per-item, so done takes a mapping or defers to the by-area routing that route_row already performs for a new row - the rule exists, it is simply not reachable from done. (2) THE DECISION, which belongs to the Owner once the mechanism can express it: for each of the seven areas, the open item that owns it now, or a statement that the area has no owner and new rows in it are unscheduled rather than silently assigned. UNTIL THEN P2.18's CLAUSES ARE DELIVERED AND THE ITEM IS NOT MARKED DONE, which is the honest state rather than either pretending the item is open work or forcing a routing nobody chose. Note the plan's own order makes the trap plain: the next open item before P2.18 is P2.17, whose subject is the round's own cost, and handing it the catalogue scatter would be absurd on its face.

items.title: No engine performs a constitutional check, so clearance gate 1 can only ever abstain and the loop withholds every emission
items.why: TRACED IN FULL IN W582, because FU-366 holds the avatar path on a condition that cannot be met by what it names. THE CHAIN, measured end to end: every cognitive engine hardcodes constitutional_validation.passed = None with the basis "no constitutional check ran: this engine performs none" - a LITERAL in the source, not a refusal; mushawara_bridge_2.deliberate reads those verdicts and derives status NOT ASSESSED whenever any is None; clearance gate 1 in avatars/core/clearance_chain.py requires status == "APPROVED" and blocks; and the recirculation loop therefore WITHHOLDS every emission. The heartbeat's own W533 comment states the outcome plainly: "six measured stages and an empty mouth is the NORMAL state of this platform today." SO THE RELEASE CONDITION FU-366 CARRIES IS WRONG, AND MEASURABLY SO. It holds "until the engines have a model path, after which clearance gate 1 can receive a constitutional verdict". MEASURED: ollama is reachable and three local models are installed (llama2, llama3.2, llama3.2:1b) with llama3.2 as the effective default - so the engines HAVE a model path - and the loop still withholds, because passed=None is a literal that no model changes. The deliberation's own reason string asserted the false cause too ("the engines refuse for want of a model path") and W582 corrected it: they do not refuse for want of a model, they perform no check at all. A hold whose condition cannot be met by the thing it names is a permanent hold wearing a temporary label. THE WORK, which is what the hold should actually wait on: implement a constitutional check that produces a REAL verdict for an emission, so gate 1 can receive a pass or a failure instead of an absence. Where it belongs is the open question and is a design decision rather than a line: either each engine performs the check its own domain supports and returns passed True or False with a basis, or - more likely right - the CHAIN performs one check over the emission and the engines stop being asked for a verdict none of them computes, which would also make the three-state derivation in deliberate honest rather than permanently NOT ASSESSED. WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, TWO THINGS ARE NOT NEGOTIABLE: the check must be able to FAIL and be seen to fail, driven both ways, because a gate that can only abstain is the same defect in a new place; and a withheld emission must continue to show the withholding as a refusal with its reason and never as an empty answer. SCOPE NOTE: this does not require a model to answer, and it is not the avatar path. It is the one thing standing between a loop that measures six stages and a loop that can emit, and FU-366's hold-or-wire choice only becomes a real question once it exists.

items.title: A fitness mean published as a vital sign averages across three provenances and reports none of them
items.why: The genome records keep a three-state provenance for every fitness and the published MEAN discards it. MEASURED IN W584 BEFORE BUILDING, and my first reading was wrong in the opposite direction so both are recorded here. organism/genome.py:194 writes "fitness_score": fitness if fitness is not None else 0.5, which looks like a default masquerading as a measurement - but the very next line writes fitness_provenance and it is HONEST: "ai-declared (unverified)" when a FITNESS line was parsed, "default-unencoded (no FITNESS line parsed)" when it was not, and "inherited-mean-unevaluated (no selection step exists)" for a crossover child. Three provenances, each naming exactly what its number is worth. Patching that writer would have broken working code. THE DEFECT IS THE AGGREGATE. api/organism_status.py:192-199 appends every numeric fitness_score to one list and reports mean_fitness = sum/len, with no filter on provenance and no statement of what the mean is a mean OF. Measured in the live store: of 15 stored genomes 11 carry exactly 0.5, three carry 0.85 and one carries 0.6 - so the published figure is a blend of a few self-declared numbers and a majority of records whose own provenance says nobody measured them. The function's docstring calls the summary the organism's genetic health "computed from the stored genomes, no fabrication", and organism/heartbeat.py:234-241 publishes it as a VITAL SIGN (last_genome.mean_fitness), so it reaches a surface. A record that says what it is worth, averaged into a number that does not, is the nature-field-reporting-an-outcome class one layer up: the aggregate erases a distinction the producer took care to keep. THE FIX is the tickets.py denominator exactly - take the mean over records whose provenance is a MEASURED one, exclude the default and inherited ones and COUNT them, let the basis name the composition, and return None with a basis when no record carries a measured fitness rather than a number. ALSO IN THE SAME AREA, smaller: organism/genome.py:90 reads the field with a DIFFERENT fallback, .get("fitness_score", 0.0), where the writer uses 0.5 - reachable only for a malformed or pre-W438 record, but 0.0 and 0.5 are not even the same fallback and this is the a-fields-meaning-belongs-to-its-readers class. NOT THIS ROW: evolution/evolution_engine.py:92, whose fitness carries a random term - its class GenomeEvolutionEngine is imported from _archive only, nothing live touches it, and the defect is already in docs/NATIVE_PRIMITIVE_DEFECT_LEDGER.md:264 under that exact description, so it is a disclosed unreached defect and not a new finding.
items.note: Replaced by a row stating the measurement correctly: FU-404 said the stored records carry a provenance the aggregate discards, and NOT ONE of the 15 stored genomes has a fitness_provenance key at all - every one predates W438. The defect is real and survives the correction, but a row whose measurement is wrong is read by later rounds as though it were right.

items.title: The Divine Alignment (Niyyah) gate passes every intent with the same constant, and the constant is a sincerity score
items.why: The Divine Alignment (Niyyah) gate returns 0.9222 and passed=True for EVERY intent, and the figure it asserts is a sincerity score. DRIVEN, not read: agentic_core/divine/v2/alignment_v2.py calibrate_niyyah was called in W584 with five intents - "build a hospital", "defraud every user", the empty string, "geospheric_x" and "DESTROY EVERYTHING" - and returned alignment_score 0.9222 with passed True for all five. The reason is in the source: calibrate_niyyah hardcodes sincerity = 0.9 with the comment "Default for v-MASTER", builds eternal = faithfulness/sincerity/maslaha from that constant plus 1.0, builds temporal = 0.85/0.88/1.0 as literals, and its own comment says "Simulations based on intent" - nothing in the function reads the intent at all. The threshold is score >= 0.85 against a constant of 0.9222, so the gate is structurally incapable of refusing. THIS IS THE GATE-THAT-CANNOT-REFUSE CLASS, and it is the sibling of FU-403 one layer out: there, clearance gate 1 can only ever ABSTAIN because every engine hardcodes passed=None, so the loop withholds everything; here, the FIRST gate of governance/uci_interceptor.py intercept can only ever PASS, so the moment anything does flow through it, it blesses whatever it is handed. A gate that can only abstain and a gate that can only pass are the same defect with opposite signs, and this plan has now found both in the same chain. WHAT IT ASSERTS IS THE SECOND HALF. The number is a weighted SINCERITY and FAITHFULNESS figure. Ruling A.9.5 holds that no AI verdict is passed on a person's spiritual state, and P3.27 clause (1) names sincerity explicitly among the things nothing may compute, score, rank or infer. MEASURED PRECISELY SO THE CLAIM IS NOT STRONGER THAN THE FACT: the subject of this call is an ACTION, not a person - uci_interceptor passes context["intent"] and biomimicry/cycles/utils.py passes a string like "geospheric_<funcname>" - so A.9.5's prohibition on judging a PERSON is not breached by the subject. What is breached is the principle underneath it: a spiritual quality is being quantified at all, the quantity is a literal, and a governance gate is built on it. A platform that may not score a person's sincerity should not be scoring sincerity as such and calling the constant a measurement. REACH, measured rather than assumed: the interceptor is driven by the suite at several points and sits on the avatars to recirculation_orchestrator to uci_interceptor import chain, so it is live code on a live path - but what reaches a person through it today is bounded by FU-403, since the recirculation loop withholds every emission. So no user action is currently being blessed by this gate, and every user action would be the moment FU-403 is fixed. The second call site is worse in a different way: biomimicry/cycles/utils.py:58-64 checks the calibration and, on failure, logs and PROCEEDS, with a comment saying "In a strict environment, we would raise an error here" - so even if the score could fail, that leg would not stop anything. THE WORK: the gate must be able to refuse and be seen to refuse, driven both ways, or it must be removed rather than left as a constitutional ornament. If a niyyah check is to exist it needs an input it actually reads and a basis it can state; if it cannot have one, the honest form is a REFUSAL to assess - NOT_ASSESSABLE with a reason, exactly as the vbs/quality.py screen does - and never a 0.9222 that reads as a measured pass. Either way the sincerity arithmetic goes: a weighted mean of literals is not a reading of anyone's or anything's sincerity.

items.title: Two live classes are both named UnifiedConstitutionalInterceptorV16Omega, and only one is the wired engine
items.why: Two live classes are both named UnifiedConstitutionalInterceptorV16Omega, and only one of them is the wired constitutional engine. MEASURED IN W584 while fixing the niyyah gate, and it nearly sent the fix to the wrong file. agentic_core/gaas/v5/uci_v16_omega.py:62 and agentic_core/governance/uci_interceptor.py:20 declare classes with the identical name. They are not variants of one thing: the gaas/v5 one is exported from agentic_core/gaas/v5/__init__.py, is what the suite drives (it returns an InterceptionResult with .status, .output and .ueg_logged, and tests monkeypatch it on the g5 module at four separate points), and is the constitutional interceptor engine the platform describes as wired. The governance one returns a plain dict, raises PermissionError from its gates, and is imported by exactly one live module - agentic_core/avatars/core/recirculation_orchestrator.py:24. WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING UNTIDY. A round reading a finding about "the interceptor" has no way to tell which file is meant, and the two have DIFFERENT GATES: the governance one carries the Divine Alignment (Niyyah) gate that FU-406 found could only ever pass, and the gaas/v5 one does not. A fix applied to the name rather than to the file would have landed in the wrong place and reported success, and a guard asserting a property of "the interceptor" can pass against one while the other breaches it. This is the naming-hazard class the Vision 8.0 assessment already flagged twice in other forms, and the grep-the-call-not-the-method-name class: a search for the class name returns both, and a reader resolves the ambiguity by guessing. THE WORK, and it is a judgement rather than a rename to be done blindly: establish which one is the constitutional interceptor for this platform and give the other a name that says what it actually is - the governance one is really the avatar recirculation path's own pre-flight, since that is its only live caller - or, if the two are meant to be one thing, say which survives and move the gates that matter into it through Change Control. NOT A ROUND'S DECISION TO MAKE SILENTLY: both are reached, one by the suite and one by an import chain, so a rename touches live paths and the choice of which name means what is an architectural statement rather than a tidy-up. What a round CAN do without deciding anything is make the ambiguity impossible to walk into: a guard that asserts there is exactly one class by that name in the live tree would have failed the moment the second appeared.

items.title: A VSB records no parent and no lineage, which is the precondition for every clause of turnover
items.why: A VSB records no parent and no lineage at all, which is the precondition for every clause of turnover. SPLIT OUT OF FU-312 IN W584, because FU-312 carried two subjects and only one of them was P3.27's. FU-312 read "Three dead genome stubs should be deleted, and a VSB records no lineage": the stubs are clause (6) of P3.27 and were deleted in W584, and the lineage half is P3.26 clause (1) word for word - "a LINEAGE field exists on an entity and is written by whatever creates it: a guard drives a creation and reads the parent back, and an entity with no parent says so rather than showing null as though it were an answer". An item closes on its own bar, and P3.27's bar says nothing about lineage, so closing FU-312 against it would have closed a row on a clause that never asked for it. MEASURED IN W584: agentic_core/api/vsb.py contains exactly one occurrence of the word lineage, a comment at line 454 about manifest versioning, and no parent_vsb, parent_id or lineage field exists on an entity anywhere in the establishment path. So an entity created by this platform records nothing about where it came from. WHY IT IS THE PRECONDITION rather than one clause among seven: P3.26 couples destruction with creation, and five of its clauses are about an entity's relationship to another entity - mitosis creating a subsidiary that inherits its parent's constitution verbatim and is funded from the parent's own share, apoptosis returning what a retired entity held to the reservoirs, the never-auto-retire set protecting the LAST entity in its realm and domain, meiosis producing a candidate that is not a birth. None of those can be driven, asserted or even stated without a parent field, because each one is a claim about a lineage. P3.26's own text says so: a VSB "records no parent and no lineage at all, which is the precondition for any of it". THE WORK: a lineage field on an entity, written by whatever creates it, never defaulted - and an entity with no parent must SAY it has none rather than carrying a null that reads as an answer, which is the three-state rule this plan applies everywhere else. The guard drives a creation and reads the parent back, and drives a parentless creation and reads the statement back.
